title: Quantized TotalSegmentator for Fast Abdominal Organ Segmentation on CPUs
abstract: BACKGROUNDTotalSegmentator is designed for a graphics processing unit (GPU), runs slowly on a central processing unit (CPU), and depends on Python, limiting CPU-only clinical deployment. OBJECTIVEThe purpose of this study was to evaluate whether TS-Portable, a self-contained CPU executable running 8-bit integer (INT8)-quantized TotalSegmentator models, is noninferior to the reference implementation across 15 abdominal organs in an external multicenter cohort, quantify CPU-only runtime, and demonstrate spleen volumetry on a picture archiving and communication system (PACS) reading station. METHODSThis retrospective study compared TS-Portable with the reference Python implementation on 100 external multicenter CT scans and 28 chronic liver disease series. Per-case mean Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and 3-mm normalized surface distance (NSD@3 mm) across 15 organs (1.5-mm resolution) and spleen-only mode were tested against a 0.01 noninferiority margin (paired bootstrap 95% CIs). Workstation and PACS runtimes were recorded; spleen volumes were compared via Lins concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTSThe external cohort included 100 patients (53 men, 47 women; mean age, 53 {+/-} 16 [SD] years). Across 15 organs, TS-Portable was noninferior for mean DSC (difference, 0.00017; 95% CI, 0.00003-0.00031; p < .001) and NSD@3 mm (difference, 0.00015; 95% CI, -0.00002 to 0.00031; p < .001) and in spleen-only mode (both p < .001). Workstation 1.5-mm median runtime was 48.0 seconds for TS-Portable on CPU versus 342.5 seconds on CPU (ratio, 7.14) and 61.5 seconds on GPU (ratio, 1.28) for the reference. On PACS, CPU spleen volumetry took 5.8 versus 43.4 seconds, agreeing with the reference (CCC, 0.9999; bias, 0.2%; 95% limits of agreement, -7.2% to 7.6%) and manual contours (CCC, 0.989; bias, -6.8%). In 28 chronic liver disease series, TS-Portable ran from DICOM in 6.5 seconds (median), agreeing with the reference (CCC, 0.99999) and manual contours (CCC, 0.992; bias, -3.4%). CONCLUSIONTS-Portable achieved noninferior abdominal organ segmentation accuracy compared with the reference implementation while running faster on a workstation CPU than the reference on a GPU. CLINICAL IMPACTSelf-contained deployment enables fast multiorgan segmentation on CPU-only computers and spleen volumetry within seconds on a standard reading station, without dedicated GPUs or software installation. HighlightsO_ST_ABSKey FindingC_ST_ABSAcross 100 external multicenter CT examinations, a quantized, self-contained CPU executable of TotalSegmentator was noninferior to the reference implementation for 15-organ segmentation accuracy and 7.14-fold faster on a workstation CPU, and completed reading-station spleen volumetry in a median of 5.8 seconds. ImportanceCompiling and quantizing three-dimensional segmentation models into a standalone CPU executable removes GPU and software-installation barriers, enabling rapid quantitative CT analysis on standard clinical workstations.

title: Quantifying Localized Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocytes by Deep Learning on H&E Images: Analytical Validation and Prognostic Value in Lung Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are a critical determinant of response to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, assessing the clinical utility of TIL quantification is challenging due to subjective manual scoring and differences in methodology, including some that may obscure localized immune responses critical to ICI response. Together, these issues limit our understanding of potential prognostic benefits of performing routine TIL quantification. Here, we present the “focal TIL score,” an artificial intelligence-powered biomarker derived from routinely generated Hematoxylin & Eosin (H&E) pathology images which measures TIL density within tiles across the entire relevant tissue region in order to account for spatial heterogeneity of localized lymphocytic infiltration. Underlying this method are two deep learning models that ensure accurate, reproducible, and interpretable quantification: one for lymphocyte detection trained on IHC-derived ground truth, and one for segmentation of tumor and tumor-adjacent stroma region (“scorable region”) trained on consensus pathologist annotations. We performed an analytical validation of the two models, demonstrating high overall performance: lymphocyte model concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) = 0.90, scorable region model Dice score = 0.87. We then performed a prognostic association study in a cohort of 685 ICI-treated LUAD patients and saw that, the focal TIL score was significantly associated with overall survival (HR=0.60, 95% CI 0.48-0.75, P<0.001), outperforming the standard biomarker PD-L1. Our findings show that quantifying the spatial intensity of immune infiltration, rather than the global average, provides a superior measure of the anti-tumor immune response. The accessibility and standardization associated with this approach may enable further studies and developments in precision oncology for LUAD.

title: Real-World Effectiveness of Osteoporosis Treatments on Bone Strength and the Impact of Sequential Anabolic Therapy
abstract: Summary In this real-world biomechanical CT analysis study, romosozumab showed greater increases in vertebral bone strength and density than teriparatide and denosumab in treatment-naïve women with postmenopausal osteoporosis. Romosozumab also increased bone strength after prior teriparatide, whereas twice-weekly teriparatide failed to maintain gains achieved with prior romosozumab. Purpose Evidence regarding the comparative effectiveness of osteoporosis treatments in improving bone strength in clinical practice remains limited. This real-world study compared the effectiveness of different osteoporosis treatments in women with postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMO), including treatment-naïve patients initiating Romo, TPTD, or DMAb (Study 1) and patients switching from one anabolic therapy to another (Study 2). Methods Japanese women with PMO aged >55 years were included. In Study 1, 57, 34, and 50 women received Romo, TPTD, or DMAb, respectively, for 12 months. In Study 2, 16 received Romo for 12 months after TPTD (TPTD-Romo) and 29 received twice-weekly TPTD for 12 months after Romo (Romo-TPTD). The primary and secondary endpoints were average percent change from baseline at 12 months in vertebral bone strength and volumetric BMD (vBMD), respectively, assessed using biomechanical CT analysis (BCT). Results At baseline, overall bone strength and vBMD were comparable across groups in both studies. In Study 1, average percent change (95% CI) in vertebral strength was highest with Romo (39.5% [34.2, 44.7]), followed by TPTD (24.4% [18.8, 30.0]), and DMAb (10.9% [7.6, 14.2]). In Study 2, vertebral strength increased by 16.1% (10.6, 21.6) with TPTD-Romo, and decreased by 7.7% ( 10.7, 4.6) with Romo-TPTD despite subsequent TPTD treatment. Similar trends were observed for vertebral vBMD. Conclusion In this real-world BCT study, Romo showed greater increases in both vertebral bone strength and density versus TPTD and DMAb in treatment-naïve women with PMO. Among prior TPTD, Romo further increased bone strength and density; however, twice-weekly TPTD failed to maintain the gains following prior Romo.

title: Motion-robust high-resolution 3D-GRASE pseudo-continuous ASL perfusion imaging at 3T
abstract: PurposeHigh resolution arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based perfusion imaging is desirable for many applications but suffers from low SNR and motion sensitivity due to the necessity for highly segmented readouts. Acquisition and reconstruction strategies were optimized for motionrobust high-resolution pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) of the brain at 3T using segmented 3D Gradient and Spin Echo (3D-GRASE) at 2.0-mm isotropic resolution. MethodsA high-resolution 3D-GRASE pCASL sequence was implemented at 3T and evaluated with a focus on the interaction between background suppression strength and motion-corrected reconstruction, together with the fat suppression and control-tag subtraction strategies that strong suppression requires. Motion correction was performed using a novel motion-compensated (alignedSENSE-based) reconstruction that simultaneously estimates the motion and image, accounting for contrast changes between tag and control data. Eight healthy volunteers were scanned under motion-free and cued motion conditions. Image quality was assessed against motion-free reference images using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM). ResultsThe optimized acquisition-reconstruction pipeline enabled robust 2.0-mm isotropic pCASL at 3T and showed improved resistance to motion-related degradation. Strong BGS provided near-complete suppression of static tissue, and water excitation reduced lipid contamination and improved coil sensitivity estimation. The regularized alignedSENSE motion correction further improved perfusion-image quality, increasing SSIM by 18.7% under Strong BGS. ConclusionRobust high-resolution pCASL at 3T can be achieved through combined optimization of acquisition and reconstruction. The combination of Strong BGS, water excitation, reference-superimposed processing, and regularized motion correction mitigates motion-related degradation and yields higher-quality perfusion images for high-resolution ASL.

title: Revealing multiscale architecture of the intact human spine using hierarchical phase-contrast tomography
abstract: Background CT and MRI provide detailed clinical assessment of the human spine; however, their millimeter-scale spatial resolution limits direct visualization of tissue microarchitecture and interfaces. Hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) enables ex vivo non-destructive, micron-resolution imaging of intact human organs without exogenous contrast agents, extending anatomical assessment to spatial scales inaccessible to conventional clinical imaging. Purpose To evaluate the capability of HiP-CT to visualize macro- to microanatomy of an intact adult human spine ex vivo . Materials and Methods An intact spine (C1-L5) from a 62-year-old male donor without known skeletal disease was formalin-fixed and imaged by HiP-CT at the European Synchrotron. Whole-spine imaging was performed using 16.26 µm isotropic voxels, with selected regions of interest imaged using 2.2 µm voxels. Ex vivo MRI was performed for anatomical comparison. Three-dimensional segmentation and quantitative analyses included intervertebral disc (IVD) grading, annulus fibrosus fiber tracing, and vertebral trabecular micro-morphometry. Results HiP-CT enabled high spatial-resolution, multiscale imaging of the intact human spine, simultaneously visualizing vertebral bone and endplate, IVDs, spinal cord and meninges, nerve roots and ganglia, vasculature, ligaments, and musculature. Three-dimensional segmentation and virtual sectioning mapped neurovascular anatomy and vertebral vascular supply, without exogenous contrast enhancement, while preserving their relationships with surrounding tissues. Whole-spine images enabled quantitative analysis of annulus fibrosus fiber organization and vertebral trabecular microarchitecture, permitting the detection of focal posterolateral fiber disruption at the L4-L5 IVD and regional differences in trabecular architecture between cervical and lumbar vertebral bodies. Local tomography resolved annulus fibrosus lamellae, vertebral endplate Haversian systems, and facet joint hyaline cartilage at micron resolution. Conclusions HiP-CT enables non-destructive, multiscale three-dimensional imaging of the intact human spine while preserving tissue relationships across spatial scales and tissue boundaries. HiP-CT images could provide an ex vivo microanatomical reference for future correlation with clinical imaging investigations of spinal disease and in the discovery and validation of imaging biomarkers. Key results Synchrotron-based hierarchical phase-contrast tomography enables non-destructive, multiscale three-dimensional imaging of an intact adult human spine using 16.26 µm isotropic voxels, resolving both mineralized and non-mineralized tissue. Local tomography using 2.2 µm isotropic voxels reveals additional microstructural detail without exogenous contrast agents or sectioning. Whole-spine imaging enables quantitative characterization of intervertebral disc fiber architecture and vertebral trabecular morphometry, alongside visualization of neurovascular anatomy while preserving spatial relationships across the intact specimen. Summary statement Hierarchical phase-contrast tomography enables non-destructive multiscale imaging of the intact human spine, resolving microarchitecture across tissues and interfaces and providing a basis for bridging clinical imaging with underlying three-dimensional microanatomy.

title: Toward Electrical Impedance Tomography of Functional Activity in the Retina
abstract: Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) is a non-invasive electrical imaging technique that reconstructs spatial variations in tissue conductivity. Traditionally used for thoracic imaging, EIT has recently been extended to neural applications in the brain and peripheral nerves. This study investigates the feasibility of using EIT to image functional neural activity in the retina. We present computational modeling of EIT measurements for image reconstruction of small conductivity perturbations across different layers of the ex-vivo mouse retina with electrodes placed in epiretinal configuration. Experimentally, we describe the design of a multi-electrode array suitable for impedance measurements under these conditions and report preliminary recordings of light-evoked impedance changes in response to wide-field optical retinal stimulation. Our computational results suggest that small conductivity perturbations of 200µm diameter and 5% conductivity variation are experimentally detectable by high-end biopotential recording equipment and could be localized by EIT imaging within ≈13% of inter-electrode distance and ≈22% of retinal thickness, respectively. In preliminary recordings, we observed slow impedance variations of 13.0±9.3 µV (0.37±0.44%) in response to retina-wide light pulse trains, when performing impedance measurements with 10 µA applied current at 2-8 kHz. These variations were characterized by a slow time course, distinct from the fast neural EIT signals associated with action potentials, and may reflect extracellular or metabolic processes linked to retinal activation. Our modelling and technical results support the feasibility of retinal EIT, while the experimental observations are preliminary and motivate further controlled studies. Retinal EIT could significantly advance retinal electrophysiology research and prosthetic development.

title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
abstract: Background Glioblastoma is pathologically characterized by extensive pseudopalisading necrosis, a hallmark linked to therapeutic resistance and dismal prognosis. While traditionally viewed as a passive ischemic event, the precise radiogenomic drivers and spatial immune architectures orchestrating active tumor necrosis remain poorly understood. Methods We integrated macroscopic clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets (n=3,639), single-cell spatial transcriptomics, and high-resolution protein immunofluorescence (IF) assays in a novel co-mutant murine model to map the necrotic microenvironment. Results Radiomic analysis of patient MRIs demonstrated that high tumoral necrotic volume serves as a powerful independent biomarker for poor long-term survival. This macro-structural necrosis phenotype is radiogenomically driven by cell-intrinsic TP53 , PTEN , and NF1 (PPN) co-mutations. Spatial transcriptomic profiling of PPN-deficient tumors revealed distinct cellular topography, separating a proliferative, invasive niche (EGFR + SOX + , Type Inv ) from a hyper-aggressive necrotic niche (ERBB3 + , Type Nec ). Mechanistically, Type Nec cells deploy a prominent CCL5/CXCL2 chemokine milieu that actively recruits and prompts tumor-associated neutrophils to undergo neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. This overactive neutrophil infiltrate drives a feed-forward loop of intrinsic tumor necroptosis mediated by the release of the damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) protein HMGB2. This cascade could be therapeutically dismantled using targeted anti-inflammatory compounds. Finally, multi-cohort clinical validation confirmed that an HMGB2 high signature dictates a high-risk, myeloid-rich immunosuppressive microenvironment in glioblastoma patients. Conclusions Our findings redefine glioblastoma necrosis as an active, mutation-driven immunopathological process. The HMGB2-mediated DAMP necroptosis cascade and associated myeloid chemokines provide robust prognostic biomarkers and immediate therapeutic vulnerabilities to disrupt the immunosuppressive necrotic niche. Key Points Clinical Stratification via Radiomics: Preoperative MRI analysis of 1,079 glioblastoma patients establishes a necrotic core volume threshold of 18.57% as a robust, non-invasive biomarker for early survival divergence and dismal long-term prognosis. Genomic Orchestration of Necrosis: Cross-species modeling identifies a high-risk somatic PPN co-mutation profile yielding two topographically distinct niches: an invasive niche EGFR + SOX + , Type Inv ) from a hyper-aggressive necrotic niche (ERBB3 + , Type Nec ). Vascular Loop and DAMP Cascade: TypeNec cells deploy a CCL5/CXCL2 chemokine milieu driving perivascular neutrophil recruitment and MPO + CitH3 + NETosis, sparking a feed-forward loop of hypoxia and necrosis driven by tumor-derived HMGB2 high that is pharmacologically targetable. Online Key Points (85 characters) Preoperative MRI biomarker of necrotic threshold determines long-term prognosis. Cross-species co-mutation profile yielding distinct invasive and necrotic niches. N eutrophil extracellular traps spark DAMP-targetable feed-forward necroptosis loop. Importance of the Study Tumor necrosis is a hallmark diagnostic feature of glioblastoma, historically characterized as a passive consequence of local tissue ischemia. This study redefines glioblastoma necrosis as an active, genetically driven immunopathological process. By integrating macroscopic clinical MRI radiomics from over 1,000 patients with single-cell spatial transcriptomics and a novel co-mutant mouse model, we reveal that cell-intrinsic TP53 , PTEN , and NF1 co-mutations actively dictate a hyper-aggressive necrotic niche. Mechanistically, these mutated tumor cells deploy a CCL5/CXCL2 chemokine cascade to recruit neutrophils, triggering an overactive neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) and a HMGB2-mediated damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP) loop that accelerates tissue destruction and myeloid immunosuppression. Crucially, we demonstrate that this pathogenic axis can be tracked non-invasively via standard neuroimaging and pharmacologically dismantled with anti-inflammatory small molecules, providing immediate diagnostic stratifications and a brand-new therapeutic vulnerability to disrupt the glioblastoma microenvironment. Lay Summary Dead tissue zones inside glioblastoma brain tumors, known as necrosis, are tied to poor patient survival. While long believed to be an accidental result of rapid tumor growth cutting off oxygen, this study reveals that tumor cells actively trigger this cell death. Driven by specific genetic mutations, these cells release distress signals that recruit immune cells called neutrophils. These neutrophils create a destructive, inflammatory loop that worsens the disease. By combining patient MRI scans with advanced spatial tissue mapping, we show that this destructive process can be tracked non-invasively and stopped using anti-inflammatory drugs, offering a new treatment strategy.

These neutrophils create a destructive, inflammatory loop that worsens the disease. By combining patient MRI scans with advanced spatial tissue mapping, we show that this destructive process can be tracked non-invasively and stopped using anti-inflammatory drugs, offering a new treatment strategy.

title: Robot-Assisted Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Guided by Cortical Topography
abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is widely used for functional brain mapping and neuromodulation, but conventional neuronavigation systems typically rely on simplified volumetric brain models that do not fully capture subject-specific cortical geometry. We developed and evaluated a novel cortical-topography-guided framework for improving TMS planning, coil alignment, and stimulation reliability. The framework integrates an enhanced head-MRI co-registration strategy based on the iterative closest point (ICP) algorithm using a three-dimensional cortical mesh reconstructed from structural MRI. This approach was designed to improve neuronavigation by more accurately aligning the participant’s head with the MRI-derived cortical anatomy, thereby reducing co-registration error. Robot-assisted TMS (RA-TMS) was used to preserve the planned coil pose relative to cortical targets. Registration accuracy, coil alignment error, and motor-evoked potential (MEP) responses at the hand area of the primary motor cortex (M1) were evaluated and compared between RA-TMS and conventional manual TMS approach, which did not consistently preserve cortical topography-guided stimulation. ICP-based co-registration reduced the registration error between the head and MRI model from 5.83 ± 1.04 mm to 1.07 ± 0.03 mm. Compared with manual alignment, RA-TMS reduced translational error from 14.79 ± 8.03 mm to 5.22 ± 1.68 mm and rotational error from 7.01 ° ± 2.29 ° to 1.09 ° ± 0.33 ° ( p < 0.001). RA-TMS also produced larger and more consistent MEP responses than manual TMS (0.27 ± 0.05 mV vs. 0.03 ± 0.01 mV, p < 0.001). Incorporating cortical topography-guided planning, combined with refined co-registration and robotic stabilization, improves coil alignment accuracy and the reliability of stimulation outcomes.

title: HELIOS: A spatial omics-informed multi-organ cell atlas enables AI-based tumour microenvironment profiling and biomarker discovery from routine histopathology
abstract: Spatial omics defines tumour microenvironments with high biological resolution but remains difficult to scale across large clinical cohorts. We developed HELIOS (H&E Learning Informed by Omics and Spatial Profiling), which transfers spatial-omics-derived cell identities into routine haematoxylin and eosin histology for interpretable single-cell tumour microenvironment profiling. HELIOS integrates 12.9 million cells from 60 specimens across 13 tissue types and four spatial profiling platforms, spanning eight epithelial, immune, stromal, and vascular populations. The resulting multiclass detector generalised across independent histopathology benchmarks. Applied to colorectal, breast, and lung cancers, HELIOS recapitulated molecular subtype-associated microenvironment states and identified prognostic immune and stromal phenotypes. Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes were consistently associated with favourable outcomes, whereas neutrophil and fibroblast phenotypes showed cancer-specific associations. HELIOS-derived features remained prognostic after adjustment for clinicopathological and molecular variables. These findings demonstrate that spatial omics can provide scalable biological supervision for extracting clinically relevant tumour microenvironment features from routine H&E, supporting scalable risk stratification and biomarker development across clinical cohorts and retrospective pathology archives.

title: Routine Chest CTA Reliably Quantifies Left Ventricular Myocardial Mass
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Routine chest computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the primary imaging modality for thoracic aortic disease, yet cardiac information within these examinations remains underutilized. We evaluated whether left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) can be reliably quantified from routine non–electrocardiographically (ECG)-gated chest CTA and its application in thoracic aortic pathology. Methods CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection. LVMM was quantified using automated three-dimensional segmentation. In a separate 10-patient validation cohort, LVMM was compared across end-systolic, end-diastolic, and non-ECG-gated source reconstructions. CTA-derived LVMM was compared with published echocardiographic and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) reference values using Cohen’s d. Results LVMM remained stable across cardiac phases and non-ECG-gated images (mean coefficient of variation, 2.4%), whereas left ventricular volume varied substantially (36.9%). CTA-derived LVMM demonstrated small effect sizes with the Penn method ( d = 0.22) and moderate effect sizes with ASE linear ( d = 0.67), area-length ( d = 0.68), and CMR ( d = 0.63). LVMM increased through young adulthood, with minimal association with age beyond 30 years. LVMM was comparable between patients with thoracic aneurysms and normal adults (140 ± 43 g vs. 141 ± 40 g; adjusted p = 1.0) but significantly greater in acute (199 ± 61 g) and chronic (191 ± 57 g) aortic dissection (both adjusted p < 0.001). Conclusions Routine non-ECG-gated chest CTA enables reliable automated LVMM quantification without additional imaging or radiation and may facilitate large-scale investigations of ventricular remodeling in thoracic aortic disease.

title: Distinct Biomarker Signatures of CMR-Defined Myocardial Remodeling in Moderate Aortic Stenosis
abstract: Background Moderate aortic stenosis (AS) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet the myocardial response to pressure overload varies substantially between patients and is incompletely reflected by valve hemodynamics. We aimed to determine whether circulating biomarkers of myocardial stress, injury, and fibrosis associate with cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)-defined myocardial remodeling in moderate AS. Methods Eighty-nine patients with moderate AS prospectively underwent CMR (cine imaging, T1 mapping, extracellular volume fraction [ECV], late gadolinium enhancement [LGE]) with concurrent measurement of NT-proBNP, high-sensitivity troponin T, sST2, TIMP-1, and Galectin-3. Biomarker associations with the phenotype-defining CMR parameters were tested with adjustment for age, sex, and renal function and correction for multiple testing, and patients were additionally classified into 4 hierarchical remodeling phenotypes. Results Six of 20 biomarker-CMR associations remained significant after correction for multiple testing. NT-proBNP tracked LV mass index (beta=0.50), ECV (beta=0.35), and LGE burden (beta=0.43, all q<0.05). TIMP-1 and Galectin-3 were selectively associated with native T1 (both beta=0.35, q=0.012), and sST2 was inversely associated with LV mass index (beta=-0.27, q=0.046). TIMP-1 (adjusted OR 2.18 per SD, 95% CI 1.37-3.48, q=0.005) and NT-proBNP (OR 2.10, 1.19-3.69, q=0.026) increased with higher hierarchical remodeling phenotype. No biomarker was associated with echocardiographic mean gradient, peak velocity, or indexed valve area after correction. Conclusions Circulating biomarkers showed distinct associations with CMR measures of myocardial remodeling in moderate AS. Matrix-related biomarkers were associated with native T1, whereas NT-proBNP was associated across several remodeling domains. These signals were not measurably related to valve hemodynamics. Registration URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05851209 . Unique identifier: NCT05851209 . Clinical Perspective What Is New? In patients with moderate aortic stenosis, myocardial remodeling on cardiac magnetic resonance was heterogeneous, and circulating biomarkers showed distinct associations with individual remodeling domains. The matrix-related biomarkers TIMP-1 and Galectin-3 were associated with native T1, whereas NT-proBNP was associated with several remodeling domains. What Are the Clinical Implications? No biomarker was associated with echocardiographic stenosis severity, suggesting that circulating biomarkers may add information on the myocardium that valve hemodynamics do not capture. If validated in larger cohorts, matrix-related biomarkers such as TIMP-1 could help select patients with moderate aortic stenosis for advanced myocardial tissue characterization.

title: Study protocol for a prospective multicenter longitudinal cohort study on progression of moderate aortic valve stenosis — the MODAS Study
abstract: Background Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is one of the most common and prognostically relevant valvular heart diseases, with a growing global burden driven by population ageing. Prediction of disease progression from moderate to severe AS, which would be instrumental for earlier diagnosis and treatment, remains challenging. At the same time, moderate AS is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition associated with clinically relevant risk, particularly in patients with cardiac damage, heart failure, or rapid disease progression. Conventional echocardiographic parameters incompletely capture the biological heterogeneity underlying AS progression. The MODAS study was established to investigate biomarkers and mechanisms of AS progression and outcome using longitudinal multimodal phenotyping. Methods The MODAS Study is a prospective, multicenter, longitudinal observational cohort study enrolling adults with moderate calcific tricuspid AS at three tertiary heart valve centers in Germany. Participants undergo standardized baseline assessment including clinical phenotyping, laboratory testing, electrocardiography, transthoracic echocardiography, cardiac computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Biospecimens are collected for biomarker, immunologic, proteomic, and genetic analyses, including genome-wide association studies and assessment of clonal haematopoiesis. Participants are followed annually for up to 5 years with repeat clinical assessment, laboratory testing, and echocardiography. The primary endpoint is time to progression to severe AS according to 2025 ESC/EACTS guideline criteria or aortic valve replacement for severe AS, adjudicated by the local multidisciplinary Heart Team. Secondary endpoints include all-cause mortality and additional clinical outcome trajectories. Multimodal data integration will be used to develop and validate prediction models for disease progression and outcome. Discussion The MODAS Study will provide a harmonized, deeply phenotyped longitudinal dataset to improve risk stratification in moderate AS and to identify imaging, inflammatory, and genetic markers associated with rapid progression and adverse outcomes. The study is designed to support future personalized surveillance strategies, improved selection for earlier intervention, and mechanistic understanding of calcific AS progression. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05851209 . Registered on 9 May 2023.

title: Biopsy-Validated Deep Learning Mapping of Glioma Infiltration Beyond Contrast Enhancement Using Multiparametric MRI
abstract: BackgroundGlioblastoma (GBM) exhibits diffuse tumor infiltration beyond contrast-enhancing margins into FLAIR-hyperintense brain tissue, where infiltrative tumor is not visible on conventional MRI. We developed and validated the infiltrative Tumor Burden (iTB) map, a deep learning biomarker that uses multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) to identify infiltrative tumor within these non-enhancing regions. MethodsPreoperative mpMRI datasets from 80 patients with WHO grade II-IV gliomas and 24 patients with brain metastases were retrospectively analyzed. Imaging included pre- and post-contrast T1-weighted, T2-weighted, FLAIR, dynamic susceptibility contrast perfusion and diffusion MRI-derived maps (rCBV, rCBF, ADC). Spatially localized stereotactic biopsies from non-enhancing glioma regions provided histopathologic ground truth while peritumoral brain metastasis regions served as biologically grounded non-tumor controls. A 3D convolutional neural network was trained on voxel-centered mpMRI patches using patient-level cross-validation and an independent test set, with data augmentation optimized using a greedy local search strategy. ResultsModel development included 121 biopsy-localized samples from 56 glioma patients and 104 non-tumor samples from 26 brain metastasis patients. Augmentation optimization significantly improved independent test-set performance, increasing accuracy from 74.5% to 85.5% and AUC from 0.859 to 0.942 (p = 0.008). Ensemble-derived voxel-wise iTB maps demonstrated low infiltration probabilities in brain metastases and extensive regions of elevated infiltration probability in glioblastoma, consistent with expected biology. ConclusionsThe iTB biomarker generates voxel-wise maps of tumor infiltration within non-enhancing FLAIR abnormalities. Validated against image-localized histopathology and independent testing, it achieved high diagnostic performance and may improve surgical planning, radiotherapy targeting, and assessment of glioma burden.

title: Linking clinical border morphology to cell-scale growth mechanisms in melanoma: a segmentation-to-simulation alignment study
abstract: An irregular border is among the most informative visual cues for melanoma, yet the prevailing quantitative treatment of that irregularity, the box-counting fractal dimension, has rarely been connected to the cell-scale mechanism that produces it. We measured seven boundary descriptors on 1,581 lesions from the 2018 International Skin Imaging Collaboration archive segmented by an automatic thresholding route, retaining the expert ground-truth route as a sensitivity arm, and compared their medians across benign, in situ, and invasive grades. We then built a hybrid cellular automaton and swept four canonical cell-level mechanisms, scoring every simulated boundary with the same measurement code used on the patient images, before testing two mechanisms that lift the empty-neighbour division rule and aligning them to the observed malignant signature with a variance-based sensitivity analysis. The malignant signature is lobulation, not roughness: compactness rises from 1.351 to 1.810, solidity falls from 0.910 to 0.853, and convexity falls from 0.936 to 0.839 from benign to invasive lesions, with areas under the curve near 0.74, while the fractal dimension varies by only 0.024 across the three grades. All four canonical mechanisms, including loss of contact inhibition, converge on near-circular clusters at a distance of 1.147 to 1.166 from the malignant target. A long-range spatial heterogeneity in the growth rate, by contrast, reproduces the observed signature to a distance of 0.187, with the correlation length of the field, not its amplitude, the dominant parameter by total-effect index. A smooth, long-range growth-rate field is therefore sufficient to generate the lobular borders that characterise invasive melanoma, whereas the empty-neighbour assumption common to cellular automata is not. Because the winning field is imposed rather than emergent, the study resolves the alignment between border morphology and cell-scale mechanism while leaving open how such heterogeneity could arise from cell-autonomous dynamics. Author Summary Melanoma is the deadliest form of skin cancer, and clinicians have long used the raggedness of a lesion’s edge as a warning sign. Computer methods usually summarise that raggedness with a single number, the fractal dimension, which measures how much fine detail a border contains. We tested that habit on 1,581 skin lesions and found it misleading. What distinguishes malignant from benign lesions here is not fine roughness but a handful of large lobes: the outline bulges and dents at a coarse scale rather than fraying at a fine one. We then asked what kind of cell behaviour could build such a border. We grew virtual tumours using simple rules for cell division, movement, and crowding, and we measured their edges with exactly the same code we applied to the patient images. The usual suspects, namely cells that ignore crowding, migrate further, or vary in their growth, all produced smooth and round tumours. Only when we let the growth rate vary smoothly across the tumour did the simulated edge acquire the observed lobes. We could impose that variation but cannot yet explain where it comes from, and we say so. That open question is our next target.

title: Estimating glioblastoma migration-to-proliferation ratio from single time-point MRI data via radial density distribution
abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) tumors with a high migration-to-proliferation ratio ( D / k ) are associated with treatment resistance, motivating the estimation of D/k from routine pre-treatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data and the investigation of mechanisms underlying its heterogeneity across patients. Unlike previous approaches based on nested spherical approximations of enhancing and non-enhancing tumor volumes, we incorporate the spatial arrangement of the enhancing and non-enhancing tumor regions by deriving a 1D tumor density distribution from their segmentations and fitting a 1D reaction-diffusion model to estimate D / k . We achieved an error of under 5% when comparing our method to synthetic density distributions and found excellent correlation with synthetic tumor segmentations (Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) = 0.996). We then evaluated associations between patient-specific D / k values and their clinical, transcriptomic, and radiomic features. When applied to 102 pre-treatment MRI scans from the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BraTS) 2017 dataset, elevated D/k significantly correlated with reduced overall survival (log-rank p = 0.01), older age ( p = 0.04), and a trend toward lower Karnofsky Performance Status ( p = 0.059). In a subset of 91 patients with available microarray data, mesenchymal-like phenotypes consistently exhibited elevated D/k across three established molecular subtype classifications ( p = 0.013, p = 0.055, and p = 0.127). Elastic Net regularization followed by overrepresentation analysis revealed an enrichment of glycosylation-related pathways among genes associated with D/k variability ( p = 0.0123 and p = 0.0368). Furthermore, Multi-Omic Factor Analysis identified a radiomic factor correlated with D / k (r = 0.57, p = 4×10 - 9 ), with the highest-weighted features corresponding to smoothness of the non-enhancing tumor region on T2 and FLAIR. Author Summary Glioblastoma tumors vary considerably in their growth patterns, with some forming relatively compact masses while others spread more diffusely into surrounding brain tissue. These patterns can be observed in a single pre-treatment MRI scan, where enhancing and non-enhancing regions approximate tumor cell density. Our method measures average tumor density in concentric spherical shells centered on the tumor core. It then fits a radially symmetric model of tumor growth to this distribution to estimate the ratio of tumor cell migration to proliferation (D/k). We validated our method using simulated tumors with known migration and proliferation characteristics. We then applied our method to the publicly available BraTS 2017 dataset. We also used matched patient gene expression data to investigate molecular differences associated with variation in D/k. We found that tumors with higher D/k were associated with poorer overall survival and a greater tendency toward the mesenchymal molecular subtype. We also identified an association between variation in D/k and genes involved in glycosylation-related pathways. Together, these findings connect tumor growth patterns visible on MRI with patient outcomes and molecular characteristics.

It then fits a radially symmetric model of tumor growth to this distribution to estimate the ratio of tumor cell migration to proliferation (D/k). We validated our method using simulated tumors with known migration and proliferation characteristics. We then applied our method to the publicly available BraTS 2017 dataset. We also used matched patient gene expression data to investigate molecular differences associated with variation in D/k. We found that tumors with higher D/k were associated with poorer overall survival and a greater tendency toward the mesenchymal molecular subtype. We also identified an association between variation in D/k and genes involved in glycosylation-related pathways. Together, these findings connect tumor growth patterns visible on MRI with patient outcomes and molecular characteristics.

title: Ultra-high-resolution Photon-Counting CT for Leaflet-Specific Evaluation of Fibrosis and Calcification in Aortic Stenosis
abstract: Objectives Ultra-high-resolution photon-counting detector (PCD)-CT may enable leaflet-specific analysis of aortic valve fibrosis and calcification, providing insights into early aortic stenosis (AS) disease progression. This study aimed to investigate how PCD-CT leaflet-specific calcific and fibrotic volumes influence cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) leaflet mobility. Materials and methods Participants with moderate aortic AS prospectively underwent both PCD-CT (n=80) and CMR (n=58). Using PCD-CT, calcific and fibrotic volumes were segmented for right (RCC), left (LCC), and non-coronary cusps (NCC) and indexed to the aortic annulus area (ICV and IFV). CMR-derived leaflet mobility index (LMI) was assessed. Two raters compared image quality using a Likert-scale (1=poor to 5=excellent) and distinguishability of individual leaflets in PCD-CT with EID-CT (n=82). Results PCD-CT analysis showed that calcification was higher in males (e.g., ICV RCC : 15±16 vs. 4±7 µL/cm 2 ;p<0.001) while fibrosis was higher in females (e.g., IFV LCC ; 47±18 vs. 34±15 µL/cm 2 ;p=0.004) across all leaflets. Fibrocalcific ratio was higher in LCC (53±276) compared to RCC (19±48;p<0.001) and NCC (13.5±34;p<0.001). LMI of RCC was higher in females compared to men (0.66±0.21 vs. 0.38±0.33;p=0.008). LMI LCC and LMI NCC showed no sex differences. LMI RCC negatively correlated with ICV RCC (ρ=-0.64[-0.77, −0.46];p<0.001) and LMI NCC with ICV NCC (ρ=-0.69[-0.80, −0.53];p<0.001), whereas LMI LCC negatively correlated with IFV LCC (ρ=-0.35[-0.56,-0.10];p=0.007), particularly in females (ρ=-0.70[-0.89, −0.31];p = 0.003). PCD-CT yielded higher image quality (5[IQR4–5] vs. 3[3–4];p<0.001) and leaflet distinguishability (79/80[99%] vs. 42/82[51%];p<0.001) than EID-CT. Conclusions Ultra-high-resolution PCD-CT allows for leaflet-specific quantification of indexed fibrotic and calcific volume. These volumes demonstrate sex- and leaflet-specific differences that may distinctly contribute to AS pathophysiology. Key Points Detailed leaflet-level characterization of fibrotic and calcific remodeling in aortic stenosis remains limited with energy integrating CT. Photon-counting CT enabled reliable leaflet-specific quantification of fibrosis and calcification, identified sex-related tissue distribution patterns, and demonstrated associations between calcification and impaired leaflet mobility. Leaflet-specific photon-counting CT assessment may enhance our understanding of aortic stenosis progression and support more individualized imaging evaluation through improved differentiation of fibrotic and calcific valvular remodeling. title: Post-implantation 3-T MRI in patients with an epicranial stimulation device: image quality and deep learning-based electrode reconstruction
abstract: Summary We evaluated structural and functional MRI at 3 T in five patients with an implanted EASEE focal cortex stimulation system and assessed MRI-only electrode reconstruction. Image quality was evaluated visually and by comparing implant-centered and control regions using structural GM/WM signal ratios, GE-EPI signal intensity, T2*, and relative off-resonance. A deep learning pipeline trained exclusively on synthetic data estimated electrode position from T1-weighted MPRAGE images. Structural and functional acquisitions were completed in all patients without scan-related adverse events. Structural images showed clear intracranial anatomy beneath the implant without visually apparent local signal loss or distortion. GE-EPI reference images and derived maps showed no consistent local disturbance corresponding to the electrode. GE-EPI signal was numerically lower in implant-centered regions, but no imaging metric differed significantly between regions (all p > 0.05). Electrode reconstructions were anatomically plausible in all patients, with patient-specific median central electrode-to-cortical gray-matter distances ranging from 9 to 20 mm. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of post-implantation structural and functional MRI and MRI-only estimation of electrode–cortex geometry, although localization accuracy remains unvalidated. This combination provides a basis for future studies integrating patient-specific electrode geometry, electric-field modeling, and functional connectivity analyses in focal cortex stimulation with the EASEE system. Plain Language Summary The EASEE system is an implant used to stimulate a specific brain region in people with focal epilepsy. In five patients, 3-T MRI provided clear images of brain anatomy and allowed functional brain scans despite the implant, while an artificial intelligence method estimated the electrode position directly from the MRI. This approach may help assess how the electrode is positioned relative to the underlying brain without requiring an additional CT scan.

title: PedDx: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Pediatric Posterior Fossa Tumor Diagnosis with Agentic AI–Enabled Independent External Evaluation
abstract: Reliable clinical translation of diagnostic artificial intelligence (AI) requires evaluation beyond classification accuracy. We developed PedDx, a segmentation-free framework for pediatric posterior fossa tumor diagnosis using T2-weighted MRI, pretrained 3DINO representations, calibrated predictions, and confidence-based abstention. Evaluation included 492 discovery, 114 replication, 129 external validation, and 40 independently tested cases, alongside 236 out-of-distribution (OOD) cases and controlled imaging perturbations. Classification accuracy was 79.8% in replication and 81.4% in external validation, increasing to 90.5% and 88.7%, respectively, among non-abstained cases. OOD analyses revealed performance degradation and confidently incorrect predictions, while perturbation analyses identified acquisition and alignment vulnerabilities. An external institution independently executed the complete agentic workflow, successfully generating predictions and structured quality-control reports for all 40 cases, with classification accuracy of 92.5%, increasing to 97.3% among non-abstained cases. PedDx demonstrates how uncertainty assessment, failure-mode characterization, external validation, and independently reproducible, traceable reporting can collectively inform the reliability and limitations of diagnostic AI systems.

title: Multiscale Spatial Characterization of Glioma MRI with MUSE and Radiomics
abstract: Purpose Characterizing glioma heterogeneity requires measurements that retain the physical scale and orientation of intratumoral intensity dependence. We evaluate the original 3D variographic field produced by the MUSE tool (Modeling Uncertainty as a Support for the Environment) alongside directional radiomics and independent image-based molecular classification. Methods We analyzed postcontrast T1-weighted magnetic resonance images and enhancing-tumor segmentations from the public UCSF-PDGM collection. Verified MUSE outputs were available for 416 independent baseline patients, of whom 375 had paired directional gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) measurements. Each MUSE field retained 328 original experimental directional variograms with physical lag distances, semivariances, orientations, and voxel-pair support. Agreement was assessed at aligned offsets and through between-tumor comparisons. Patient-level permutation tests evaluated associations with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) status on 2,508 native direction-lag coordinates. A standalone 3D residual convolutional neural network (CNN) provided a separate IDH classification benchmark. Results At 9,371 geometrically aligned offsets, native MUSE semivariance and half GLCM contrast correlated strongly (Pearson r = 0.954). Across 31,599 eligible between-tumor comparisons, representation-level dissimilarities showed Spearman ρ S = 0.862, with sensitivity to GLCM feature family and long-offset sampling support. In 364 grade-4 tumors, including 24 IDH-mutant cases, the original MUSE field was associated with IDH after conventional adjustment (global permutation p = 0.00050), but the association was attenuated after primary directional GLCM adjustment ( p = 0.256). The independent CNN achieved an out-of-fold IDH ROC-AUC of 0.792 and PR-AUC of 0.414 across 416 patients. Native MUSE examples revealed scale- and direction-dependent spatial behavior, including distances beyond those sampled by the GLCM protocol. Conclusion Variograms by MUSE provide a physically indexed description of tumor spatial heterogeneity that can accompany radiomic analysis and CNN classification. The observed statistical overlap is substantial, and incremental clinical discrimination beyond directional GLCM features remains unestablished.

title: Development and evaluation of automated organ segmentation models for abdominal ultrasound in injured children
abstract: BackgroundAccurate organ segmentation in pediatric focused assessment with sonography in trauma (FAST) is an important prerequisite for automated image analysis and image quality assessment, but manual segmentation is time-intensive, subject to inter- and intra-observer variability, and limits the scalability of deep learning dataset development. Although deep learning has shown promise for ultrasound organ segmentation, its application to pediatric FAST has not been evaluated. ObjectiveTo describe the development and evaluation of deep learning models to automatically localize and segment six abdominal organs in pediatric FAST. MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study using a convenience sample of archived FAST examinations from 200 injured children evaluated at a Level I pediatric trauma center. Emergency ultrasound fellowship-trained physicians manually segmented six key abdominal organs. Annotated image-mask pairs were split into training and test sets in an 80:20 ratio. We developed or fine-tuned U-Net, EVIT U-Net, UltraSAM, and nnU-Net models to automatically segment the bladder, kidney, liver, spleen, spine, and diaphragm. Segmentation accuracy was assessed using the Dice-Sorensen Coefficient (DSC) compared with manual annotations. Pediatric emergency ultrasound experts reviewed previously unlabeled FAST clips and rated the acceptability of model-generated organ masks. ResultsThe dataset included 1,807 manually annotated image-mask pairs from 200 pediatric FAST clips. Using an 80:20 split with no overlap between video clips, 1,446 image-mask pairs were used for training and 361 for testing. Across all models and organs, mean DSC was 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.84). Mean DSC was highest for the kidney and bladder, each 0.91 (95% CI: 0.87-0.95), and lowest for the diaphragm at 0.63 (95% CI: 0.60-0.67). EVIT U-Net achieved the highest DSC for kidney, liver, and spleen, performed comparably to the highest-performing models for bladder, and had a mean inference time of 54 milliseconds per image. In previously unlabeled pediatric FAST clips, experts rated model-generated organ masks as acceptable for localization in 73%-95% of clips across organs. ConclusionWe describe the automatic segmentation of key abdominal organs in pediatric FAST with limited annotated data. This represents an important advancement in our image processing pipeline and can accelerate the development of large, robust datasets with segmentation for anatomy and pathology. Experts found that model-generated masks provided acceptable localization in most previously unlabeled pediatric clips, supporting the potential use of automated segmentation in pediatric FAST image analysis.

title: Blood-based biomarkers across the Alzheimer’s disease continuum in older Korean population
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (pTau217) is a robust biomarker of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology. However, whether a single biomarker can adequately capture both clinical diagnosis and disease progression remains unclear. We investigated the complementary roles of plasma AD biomarkers and routinely measured metabolic markers across different stages of AD. Methods Using the Gwangju Alzheimer’s & Related Dementia (GARD) cohort, we analyzed cross-sectional and longitudinal data, including amyloid-PET, MRI, neuropsychological examinations, and APOE genotypes. Plasma pTau217, GFAP, and NfL levels were measured alongside routine biochemical markers to evaluate their associations with pathology and neurodegeneration. Results Plasma pTau217 best identified amyloid-PET positivity (AUC > 0.91). For AD diagnosis, adding cholesterol and glucose to pTau217 improved the AUC from 0.781 to 0.873. To predict progression in amyloid-positive individuals, glucose alone outperformed pTau217 (AUC 0.840 vs. 0.747), whereas adding GFAP yielded the strongest prognostic performance (AUC 0.867). Discussion Plasma pTau217 primarily reflects amyloid pathology, whereas metabolic markers provide complementary information related to the clinical expression and progression of the disease. Integrating biomarkers across distinct biological domains may improve risk stratification and prognostic assessment in AD.

title: Claustrum Morphometry Reveals Spatially Heterogeneous Alterations in 22q11DS
abstract: Abstract. The human claustrum is a small, irregular, and complexly positioned structure, yet it carries long range projections to most cortical regions responsible for executive functioning. Prior structural MRI research has largely relied on global volume as the metric of its morphology. Such measures may obscure regionally specific morphological changes relevant to developmental and pathological variation. We therefore addressed this limitation by applying longitudinal surface-based morphometry to 874 scans from 440 individuals aged 5–35 years, comparing typical development with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (22q11DS), a genetic condition characterized by brain dysmaturation, and assessing associations with working memory performance. Our data show a significant age-related volumetric decline that is reduced in 22q11DS left claustra, while surface deformation and thickness analyses revealed spatial patterns unique to hemisphere, group, and developmental age. In controls, the claustrum surface deformed with age in clustered zones along a dorsoventral gradient, and the dorsal-anterior zone thinned across development while the ventral zone thickened. 22q11DS claustra showed less age-related deformation than controls, whose claustrum surface changes associated with verbal working memory. This structural correlate was statistically equivalent to zero in carriers, consistent with a disrupted claustral development to the working memory vulnerability of the syndrome. These findings show the value of surface-based morphometry over volume alone, highlight dysmaturation and regionally organized claustrum shape variation, and suggest that disrupted structural organization is accompanied by a weaker claustrum-working memory association.

title: QUARTZ: Cross-Dataset Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Retinal Vasculometry
abstract: Examination of retinal images provides a non-invasive means to assess the body’s microvascular system, with vessel morphology linked to ocular and systemic diseases. QUARTZ (QUantitative Analysis of Retinal vessel Topology and siZe) is an automated, artificial intelligence-enabled retinal vasculometry system designed for processing large-scale retinal image datasets, including over 4 million images from within the National Health Service, to facilitate epidemiological studies. The system is uniquely capable of extracting useful information from lower quality images, including those which are partially illuminated, enabling analysis of a greater proportion of images. To enhance cross-dataset generalisation of the system from an earlier dataset-tailored approach, this work leverages 26 annotated retinal image datasets spanning diverse demographics, diseases, camera types, and imaging protocols. Evaluation on the external EPIC-Norfolk dataset demonstrates robust performance with F1 scores of 0.8305, 0.8477, 0.8741, 0.9532, and 0.8677 for arteriole, venule, vessel, optic disc, and optic cup segmentation, respectively, and 0.9197 for image quality classification. The cross-dataset generalisation approach demonstrated increased performance for arteriole/venule segmentation and optic disc segmentation. However, improvements in performance were not observed for optic cup segmentation, or for image quality classification. An online tool is provided to support wider adoption and reproducible biomarker research across diverse populations and imaging settings. In addition, the new public CHASE-AV database is introduced for arteriole and venule segmentation.

title: Lesion selection and external evaluation of clinical-imaging survival models after transarterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BackgroundPretreatment computed tomography (CT) describes tumor characteristics in patients receiving transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but whether measuring more tumors improves mortality predictions in a new cohort remains unclear. We assessed the added value of different lesion-selection scopes beyond shared clinical predictors. MethodsWe compared a model using five clinical variables with models adding CT measurements from the largest, two largest, or all retained annotated tumors. All models used the same regularized discrete-time survival estimator. Evaluation used repeated nested cross-validation in 228 WAW-TACE patients and frozen external application in 69 HCC-TACE-Seg patients, with 15 deaths by day 365. We assessed first-year probability error, discrimination, and calibration, followed by local recalibration using small external samples. ResultsInternally, adding CT-derived lesion features did not establish an improvement in prediction accuracy. Externally, the all-lesion model had the highest discrimination point estimates, but its advantage over the clinical-only model was uncertain. Its mortality probabilities were less accurate than those of the clinical-only model, with calibration estimates consistent with overly extreme predicted risks. Local recalibration reduced its median held-out prediction error at day 365, but the median adjusted error remained higher than that of the adjusted clinical model. Simple tumor-burden predictors also did not improve external probability accuracy over the clinical baseline. ConclusionsIn these cohorts, measurements from more annotated tumors did not yield more reliable first-year mortality probabilities. Comparisons of clinical-imaging models should evaluate external probability accuracy and calibration alongside patient ranking.

Its mortality probabilities were less accurate than those of the clinical-only model, with calibration estimates consistent with overly extreme predicted risks. Local recalibration reduced its median held-out prediction error at day 365, but the median adjusted error remained higher than that of the adjusted clinical model. title: MedMLX: On-Device Medical Imaging AI for Apple Silicon
abstract: BackgroundMedical imaging research increasingly combines specialized artificial intelligence models for segmentation, detection, image synthesis and report generation. For three-dimensional CT and MRI, these workflows typically run on NVIDIA GPUs with substantial memory. On-device AI on widely available Apple Silicon computers could broaden access to these models for clinical researchers. These computers share a large memory pool between the CPU and GPU, which suits workflows that combine several models. However, few established imaging models run natively on Apple Silicon. Adapting a model to new hardware also requires verifying that its results match the original software. MethodsWe developed MedMLX, a collection of 21 established medical imaging models rewritten for Apple Silicon in MLX, Apples machine learning framework. The collection includes nnU-Net, TotalSegmentator, MedSAM2 and SAM 3. The models segment organs and tumors, detect lung nodules, generate synthetic images and draft radiology reports from CT, MRI, PET/CT, radiographs and endoscopic images. Using public cases from 11 imaging datasets, we compared the models results with those of the original software run on an Intel CPU and an NVIDIA GPU. Agreement required a Dice coefficient of at least 0.99 for every segmentation label and equivalent criteria for other outputs. We measured memory use and processing time on an Apple M1 Max computer with 64 GB of memory. ResultsMedMLX agreed with the original software in 211 of 212 comparisons. The single exception was a brain MRI segmentation. On this case, the original software itself gave different results on the two devices. We illustrated sequential workflows, including anatomical segmentation of a synthetic brain MRI and lesion synthesis guided by organ segmentation. With a memory-saving setting, 19 of the 21 models used less than 16 GB of memory. This setting reduced memory use by a median of 49% and increased processing time by a median of 13%. ConclusionsMedMLX enables on-device AI with established medical imaging models on Apple Silicon computers rather than specialized NVIDIA hardware. The models agree closely with the original software, and most need less than 16 GB of memory.

title: Matrix biophysical cues drive transient or prolonged breast cancer dormancy programmes
abstract: Breast cancer metastasis can emerge after disease-free periods through the reawakening of dormant disseminated cancer cells. Despite evidence that the extracellular matrix (ECM) modulates this phenomenon, biophysical cues regulating dormancy fate and therapeutic responses remain poorly understood. Here, we engineered stiffness-matched gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) and alginate-based 3D matrices to disentangle matrix stiffness from adhesion and degradability and uncover their contributions to dormancy. Deep learning-based 3D segmentation revealed that adhesive and degradable matrices supported rounded and proliferative tumour masses, whereas inert matrices favoured single cell dormancy. Within inert matrices, stiffness further determined dormancy fate, with soft matrices activating SOX9-associated transient stem-like dormancy, while stiff matrices reduced cell volume, increased intracellular macromolecular crowding of proteins and induced NR2F1-associated prolonged dormancy marked by autophagy and cellular stress. Transiently dormant cells retrieved from soft matrices retained dormancy memory and failed to form tumours in chicken chorioallantoic membranes, demonstrating persistence of matrix-induced states after removal of biophysical cues. Moreover, patient-derived cells in soft inert matrices recapitulated transient dormant states and exhibited therapy resistance. We demonstrate that tuneable biophysical cues shape distinct dormancy states, linking matrix mechanics to dormancy regulation and therapeutic response.

title: Fractional tumor burden refines prognostic stratification beyond MGMT status in glioblastoma after chemoradiotherapy
abstract: Background and PurposeFollowing standard-of-care treatment for glioblastoma, response to chemoradiotherapy is difficult to evaluate because changes on postcontrast T1WI may represent either treatment effect or tumor progression, particularly in the early posttreatment period. Although O6-methylguanine DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation is prognostic and informs treatment response, outcomes among patients remain heterogeneous. We hypothesized that combining advanced physiologic imaging with methylation status would improve early prognostic stratification. Materials and Methods.In this retrospective cohort study, patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma who underwent surgical resection or biopsy followed by standard chemoradiotherapy and had diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MR imaging within 6 weeks after treatment completion were included. Imaging-derived metrics included mean apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), mean standardized relative cerebral blood volume (sRCBV), change in contrast-enhancing volume on dT1, and the volume of fractional tumor burden (FTB), which is the volume of enhancing tissue with moderate-to-high probability of vascular tumor. Overall survival was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing. ResultsForty-three patients (21 male, 22 female) were included with a mean age of 57 years. Median overall survival was longer in patients with O6-methylguanine DNA methyltransferase-methylated tumors compared with unmethylated tumors (19.7 vs 10.6 months; P = .01). Stratification by mean sRCBV, mean ADC, or change in dT1 volumes was not associated with overall survival (P > .05 for all comparisons). Among unmethylated tumors, FTB <5 mL was associated with longer overall survival compared with [≥]5 mL (14.5 vs 8.4 months; P = .006), whereas no survival difference, based on FTB volumes, was observed in methylated tumors (P = .50). ConclusionsFractional tumor burden, measured within 6 weeks after chemoradiotherapy, refines prognostic stratification beyond methylation status in glioblastoma, identifying a subgroup of unmethylated tumors with longer overall survival. These findings support the use of spatially resolved perfusion imaging to improve interpretation of early posttreatment enhancement.

title: Deep learning reveals prognostic information beyond AJCC stage in routine histopathology of early-stage melanoma: the population-based D-ESMEL study
abstract: Of all melanoma patients who develop distant metastasis over time, 41% were initially diagnosed with stage I/II. More accurate prognostic models are needed to select patients for potential (neo)adjuvant therapy. We hypothesise that histopathological features in whole slide images (WSIs) from primary early-stage melanomas provide additional information beyond American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) stage. We utilised data from the population-based Dutch Early-Stage Melanoma (D-ESMEL) study. This included a discovery set (n=328) of case-control sets matched on follow-up time and known prognostic features (i.e. Breslow thickness, ulceration, age, and sex) and a validation cohort based on >5,500 patients following a nested case-control (NCC) design with stage-matched controls (n=266). We developed an end- to-end deep learning workflow to automatically extract relevant patches from WSIs and predict patient-level metastatic risk based on histopathological features independent of AJCC stage. The discovery set served as a training set for the workflow using 10-fold cross-validation. The prognostic performance of this model and its independence from clinical risk factors was evaluated in the validation cohort using odds ratios (OR) and the weighted C-index. We achieved a balanced accuracy of 0·88 (µ: 0·81; 95% CI: 0·77–0·85) in the best validation fold of the discovery set. In the validation cohort, metastatic risk predictions from the deep learning model were an independent prognostic factor (adjusted OR: 1·97; p <0·01). Combining the deep learning predictions (C-index: 0·86) with AJCC stage (C-index: 0·80) yielded the highest C-index of 0·87, significantly improving the C-index compared to AJCC stage alone ( p <0·001). Our histopathology-based deep learning model was rigorously evaluated in a population-based cohort and demonstrated added prognostic value beyond AJCC stage. Further investigations of the underlying biological features could improve clinical decision making and patient outcomes.

title: Atlas-Based MRI Spatial Phenotyping in Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma
abstract: Pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs) arise throughout the developing brain, and their anatomic distribution is related to age, molecular subtype, and extent of resection (EOR). In clinical studies, pLGG location is commonly represented by a single manually assigned anatomic category, which does not quantify the full spatial extent of tumors spanning multiple brain regions. We developed and evaluated a reproducible, publicly available pediatric atlas-based framework integrating voxel-wise probabilistic mapping with patient-level atlas-derived spatial features. In this retrospective study, preoperative MRI from 349 patients with pLGG was registered to the Haskins pediatric template using EasyReg. Probabilistic maps showed differences in tumor distribution by age, molecular subtype, and EOR, including greater optic pathway and suprasellar involvement at 0-2 years and greater cerebellar involvement in KIAA1549-BRAF fusion tumors. Atlas-derived spatial, tumor morphometric, and clinical features distinguished gross total resection/near total resection from subtotal resection or biopsy/no-surgery (Replication area under the curve, 0.864). Substituting 107 automatically computed regional overlap features for the manually assigned location variable in previously published clinico-imaging risk stratification models did not significantly alter discrimination (smallest P = 0.12). Together, these group- and patient-level analyses demonstrate the frameworks utility for quantitative spatial phenotyping in imaging and clinical studies of pLGG.

title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Regional Myocardial Flow Reserve Beyond Global Flow and Perfusion: REFINE PET
abstract: Background The incremental prognostic value of regional myocardial flow reserve (MFR) assessed by positron emission tomography (PET) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) beyond global MFR remains unclear. We sought to evaluate the prognostic value of regional MFR in the international multicenter REFINE PET registry. Methods This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 35,391 patients from 13 sites in the international REFINE PET registry who underwent rubidium-82 ( 82 Rb) and 13 N-ammonia ( 13 NH 3 ) PET MPI. Abnormal MFR was defined as <2.0. Patients were classified into three groups: MFR-Group 1 (normal global and regional MFR; n=19,744), MFR-Group 2 (normal global MFR but abnormal regional MFR; n=3,184), and MFR-Group 3 (abnormal global and regional MFR; n=12,463). Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) included all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, late revascularization (>90 days), and hospital admission for unstable angina. Results During a mean follow-up of 4.0 ± 2.9 years, 9,903 patients (28.0%) experienced MACE. Annualized MACE rates increased stepwise across MFR-Groups 1-3 (4.0%/year, 7.5%/year, and 11.8%/year, respectively; p <0.001). Abnormal regional MFR independently predicted MACE after adjustment for clinical risk factors, global MFR, and stress total perfusion deficit (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.25–1.43). Adding regional MFR to a model including global MFR significantly improved model fit (χ² 4,784 to 4,871; p <0.001), discrimination (AUC 0.710 to 0.729; p <0.001), and reclassification (NRI 41.9%). Among patients with normal perfusion and preserved global MFR, abnormal regional MFR identified higher risk (5.0%/year vs. 2.8%/year; p <0.001). Conclusions Regional MFR provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional PET MPI findings, including global MFR, and may refine risk stratification, particularly when global MFR is preserved. However, regional abnormalities in MFR may be overlooked when global MFR is preserved. In this international multicenter study of 35,391 patients, abnormal regional MFR was independently associated with major adverse cardiovascular events and provided incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical and PET-MPI findings, including global MFR and myocardial perfusion abnormalities. Importantly, even among patients with normal perfusion and preserved global MFR, those with abnormal regional MFR had a substantially higher annualized event rate than those with normal regional MFR (5.0% versus 2.8%). These findings highlight the importance of assessing regional MFR in addition to global MFR during routine PET-MPI interpretation. Graphic Abstract

title: Neural shape models enable cohort-scale simulation of knee cartilage mechanics
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis affects over 350 million people worldwide, is a leading cause of disability, and carries substantial costs. Cartilage mechanical load is believed to play a critical role in osteoarthritis pathophysiology, yet clinical biomechanics research uses external measures of joint loading that do not capture tissue-level load. We developed a fully-automated pipeline that builds biomechanical knee models from a single MRI using deep learning-based segmentation and neural shape models, and elastic foundation contact to simulate gait. Applied to 756 knees from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, each simulated under the same 10 standardized gaits, the pipeline converged in 99.6% of 7,560 simulations. Medial tibial pressure decreased from healthy to incident to mild osteoarthritis as disease-related shape changes enlarged contact area, an effect reproduced in simulations of synthetic knees. Yet within knees, medial cartilage thinned fastest over six years in regions of highest pressure, with stronger relationships in incident and mild osteoarthritis knees. Automated simulations provided cohort-scale, tissue-level support for mechanical theories of osteoarthritis progression and a framework for prospectively quantifying cartilage load to guide mechanical interventions.

title: Morphometric Analysis of Mandibular Incisors with Single Canal Systems Using A Developmental Automated Computational Framework.
abstract: Objective This study developed a computer vision-based framework for quantitative morphometric analysis of mandibular incisors with single root canals using axial video data obtained from micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). Methods Fifty extracted micro-CT scanned single-rooted mandibular incisors with single root canals (coded 1TN1 according to Ahmed et al. coding system) were included. After segmentation of the pulp space, video recordings were constructed using Mimics. The video frames were preprocessed through Gaussian filtering and segmented in the hue, saturation and value/brightness colour space domain. The contours were fitted with ellipses to compute morphometric descriptors, including aspect ratio (AR), roundness (R) and form factor. Aspect ratio-based classification was used to categorise canal cross-sections into 4 types (Round, Oval, Long Oval and Flattened). Automated AR measurements were validated against manual reference measurements of the same parameter at the cemento-enamel junction in 30 specimens, using Passing-Bablok and Deming regression, Bland-Altman analysis and the intraclass correlation coefficient; R and FF were not subjected to formal method comparison. Longitudinal trends along all thirds were visualised, and similarity measurement-based grouping comparisons were performed using dynamic time warping (DTW) clustering algorithm. Results The automated framework successfully processed 8334 axial frames. Within each root third, DTW clustering of AR trajectories resolved 3 morphological strata. Cluster 1 represented canals with the highest R (mean = 0.82) and lowest AR (mean = 1.39). Cluster 2 showed moderate ovality, while Cluster 3 exhibited the most complex morphology with the highest AR (mean = 2.84) and lowest R (mean = 0.40). Only 17 of the 50 specimens (34%) retained the same stratum in all 3 root thirds (mean adjusted Rand index 0.176), indicating that a canal's morphological class frequently changes along the root. Morphometric analysis revealed that canal complexity and flattening reached their peak in the middle third of the root. Conclusion This study introduces a robust and fully automated framework for quantitative assessment of canal morphology using axial videos. The findings highlight that mandibular incisors often harbour significant morphological complexity in the middle third, which may challenge standard instrumentation.

title: Application Value of Cochlear Size Assessment in Cochlear Implantation Surgery.
abstract: Background Numerous studies using 3D Slicer have enhanced the authors' understanding of anatomical variations in the inner ear. Yet, there is no single report that has analyzed the correlation between cochlear size and cochlear duct length. Methods High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) images of 164 structurally normal cochleae underwent reconstruction and threshold segmentation. The reconstructed images yielded measurements of values A, B, C, and D, cochlear height (CH), total cochlear duct length (CDL), length of the 1/2 basal turn (180° CDL), and full length of the basal turn (360° CDL). These cochlear parameters were analyzed and compared between patients with sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) and individuals with normal bone-conduction (NBC) hearing. Results In this study, 82 ears were included in patients with SNHL, the same quantity as NBC cochlear. Age and side showed no significant effect on cochlear dimensions, with males exhibiting larger cochleae than females in both groups. Except for C-value and 180° CDL, all other cochlear parameters differed between groups, indicating a degree of micro-malformation in cochleae of SNHL patients. The A-value, B-value, and CH all showed a positive correlation with cochlear duct length, and the highest correlation was observed for the B-value. Conclusion Patients with SNHL are usually accompanied by varying degrees of mild cochlear deformity. The difference in the size of the cochlea between individuals suggests the need for personalized cochlear implantation. The A, B, and D values and CH measurement values can predict CDL, thus guiding the determination of the best implant electrode insertion depth.
