title: Pediatric Leptomeningeal Glial Tumors: A Retrospective Case Series and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Objective Diffuse leptomeningeal glioneuronal tumor (DLGNT), including primary diffuse leptomeningeal oligodendroglial tumors (PDLOs) and leptomeningeal spread of high-grade gliomas, are rare pediatric neoplasms with diffuse leptomeningeal dissemination and limited parenchymal involvement. Their often nonspecific neurological symptoms frequently lead to misdiagnosis as infectious or inflammatory meningitis, complicating early identification. Methods To investigate these diagnostic challenges, the authors retrospectively reviewed the records of 4 pediatric patients (2-13 years) diagnosed with leptomeningeal glial tumors over a 5-year period. Clinical features, neuroimaging, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings, histopathology, treatment, and outcomes were analyzed. Results All patients had subacute or chronic neurological symptoms, including gait ataxia (4/4), motor weakness (3/4), headache or vomiting (3/4), cognitive or behavioral decline (3/4), and seizures (2/4). Cerebrospinal fluid abnormalities contributed to diagnostic confusion but were not identical across all cases: pleocytosis was present in all patients, elevated protein was documented in those with available protein measurements, and reduced or relatively low glucose was observed only in some patients. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated diffuse leptomeningeal involvement along the neuraxis in all patients, with cystic/nodular T2-hyperintense lesions and variable enhancement. Three patients were diagnosed within the DLGNT/PDLO spectrum and 1 with high-grade glioma with leptomeningeal dissemination. Hydrocephalus requiring ventriculoperitoneal shunting developed in 3/4 patients. All received chemotherapy; 1 required decompressive spinal surgery and craniospinal radiotherapy. At last follow-up, 3 patients were alive with neurological sequelae and 1 had died of progressive disease. Conclusion These findings highlight that pediatric leptomeningeal glial tumors are diagnostically challenging and easily mistaken for chronic meningitis. Characteristic MRI findings, elevated CSF protein, and spinal dissemination are important clues.

title: An Extensive Tail Sign in Primary Thoracic Myxofibrosarcoma: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Myxofibrosarcoma is a malignant soft tissue tumor of fibroblastic origin, occurring mainly in the extremities but extremely rarely in the thoracic trunk. Myxofibrosarcoma typically appears as a slow-growing, painless mass but features a frequent local recurrence due to microscopic extension beyond visible margins. On MRI, the "tail sign"-which indicates subtle spread along the fascial plane-is known to be a potential risk factor for recurrence. Case presentation The patient was a 73-year-old woman complaining of continuous right back pain. Chest CT showed a poorly contrast-enhanced mass involving the 5th and 6th right ribs, as well as a separate nodule. The biopsy confirmed a diagnosis of myxofibrosarcoma. The mass exhibited hypointensity on T1-weighted images and hyperintensity on T2-weighted images on MRI; on contrast-enhanced T1-weighted images and STIR images, a tail sign extending toward a small satellite nodule was observed. The patient underwent an extended resection involving the 5th through 7th ribs. A total of 61.2 Gy radiation was irradiated to the paravertebral region neighboring the tumor where the surgical margin was poor. A local recurrence was detected in the anterolateral region of the tumor resection site 5 months after surgery. The patient was treated with sequential chemotherapy using doxorubicin, eribulin, and pazopanib and is alive at 26 months after surgery without distant metastasis. Conclusions The current case exemplifies the aggressive local behavior of thoracic myxofibrosarcoma, especially when a long tail sign appears.

title: Hepatic Metastasis of Meningioma Treated with Partial Hepatectomy: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Meningioma is one of the most common central nervous system tumors; however, metastatic lesions are extremely rare. Particularly, hepatic metastasis from meningioma is uncommon, and its diagnosis and optimal management remain undefined. Case presentation A 70-year-old man with a history of left parietal meningioma resection in 2011 and gamma knife therapy for recurrence in the left lateral ventricle in June 2025. A PET-CT scan performed for cancer screening in June 2025 revealed abnormal fluorodeoxyglucose uptake in segment 8 of the liver, with a maximum standardized uptake value of 6.2. CT, and MRI revealed multiple hepatic masses. All tumor markers were within normal ranges. A percutaneous liver biopsy indicated a spindle cell tumor; however, the diagnosis remained inconclusive. For diagnostic and therapeutic purposes, partial hepatectomy of segments 6 and 8 and cholecystectomy were performed. Histopathological examination revealed proliferating spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in fascicles. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for vimentin, epithelial membrane antigen, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming the diagnosis of hepatic metastasis from meningioma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged in good condition. Conclusions Hepatic metastasis from meningioma is extremely rare; however, it should be considered in the differential diagnosis of hepatic tumors in patients with a history of meningioma. Surgical resection is valuable in establishing a definitive diagnosis and achieving local disease control.

title: A Case of Primary Leiomyoma of the Chest Wall Showing High Uptake on FDG-PET.
abstract: Introduction Primary leiomyoma of the chest wall is a rare entity. We report a case of primary chest wall leiomyoma with intense uptake on fluorodeoxyglucose PET (FDG-PET), requiring differentiation from malignancy. Case presentation An 82-year-old man with a history of asbestos exposure underwent annual chest CT surveillance. A 19-mm nodule was newly identified on the right chest wall and had not been present on CT the previous year. Although the lesion had well-defined margins on CT, FDG-PET demonstrated intense uptake with a maximum standardized uptake value of 11.8, raising suspicion for malignancy. Surgical resection was performed for diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. Histopathological examination revealed fascicular proliferation of spindle-shaped cells. Immunohistochemical analysis suggested a smooth muscle tumor, and retention of BRCA1-associated protein 1 and methylthioadenosine phosphorylase excluded mesothelioma. Based on these findings, the tumor was diagnosed as a primary leiomyoma of the chest wall. Conclusions Primary leiomyomas of the chest wall are rare and may show high FDG uptake on PET imaging, making differentiation from malignant tumors challenging. A comprehensive evaluation incorporating imaging, intraoperative findings, and pathological assessment is essential for accurate diagnosis.

title: Small Bowel Volvulus Diagnosed and Treated Using Intraoperative Angiography in a Hybrid Operating Room: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Small bowel volvulus is a surgical emergency that may cause mesenteric ischemia; however, diagnosis may be difficult when bowel perfusion appears preserved. Case presentation An 84-year-old man presented with recurrent postprandial abdominal pain and melena 6 months after a total pharyngolaryngectomy with a jejunal free flap reconstruction. Extensive endoscopic evaluations, including capsule endoscopy, revealed no bleeding source. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed the whirl sign at the root of the small-bowel mesentery with the narrowing of the superior mesenteric artery (SMA), while bowel wall enhancement was preserved. Because the symptoms recurred after resuming oral intake, a hybrid surgery combined with angiography was planned for both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. The SMA angiography demonstrated significant stenosis without apparent bowel hypoperfusion. After the intra-arterial administration of alprostadil, distal mesenteric perfusion deteriorated on the angiography, and laparoscopic exploration revealed ischemic changes consistent with small bowel volvulus. Because laparoscopic reduction was difficult, an open reduction was performed. Repeat angiography confirmed the resolution of the SMA narrowing and the restoration of distal flow. The patient's symptoms resolved completely. Conclusions The hybrid surgery enabled a functional assessment of mesenteric hemodynamics and immediate surgical treatment during a single procedure. It may be useful in selected patients with small bowel volvulus who have preserved bowel perfusion at rest but recurrent symptoms suggestive of intermittent mesenteric ischemia, and in whom the indication for surgical detorsion remains uncertain.

title: A Case of a Cardiac Re-Rupture Caused by the Removal of Pericardial Patches Late after a Sutureless Repair for a Cardiac Rupture.
abstract: Introduction Surgical treatment is the only reliable therapeutic option for a left ventricular free wall rupture (LVFWR). There are 2 major surgical techniques, namely, sutureless repair and sutured repair; a ventricular pseudoaneurysm is a late postoperative complication. We herein report a case of a re-ruptured left ventricular pseudoaneurysm after a sutureless bovine pericardial patch repair. Case presentation The patient was a 79-year-old woman who underwent a sutureless pericardial patch repair for a blow-out-type left ventricular rupture following an anterior myocardial infarction 10 months previously. She was referred to Fujita Health University Okazaki Medical Center with a diagnosis of thoracic empyema and a suspected pericardial patch infection. Pleural effusion was positive for a few Streptococcus agalactiae . Coronary CT revealed the occlusion of the proximal left anterior descending branch and aneurysmal dilatation of the anterolateral wall of the left ventricle covered with pericardial patches. The operation was performed via a left fifth intercostal thoracotomy without cardiopulmonary bypass. The covering bovine pericardial patches and felt strips were easily removed, and the omental flap was secured in place. However, an emergency reoperation was necessitated for a left hemothorax 3 hours after surgery. Active bleeding was observed from the aneurysmal area, which had been previously covered with pericardial patches. After inducing deep hypothermia of 20°C, the fragile tissue surrounding the bleeding site was debrided under ventricular fibrillation. A 3 × 3-cm myocardial tissue defect was observed and closed using a bovine pericardial patch (Model 4700; Edwards Lifesciences, Irvine, CA, USA) with ten 2-0 MH U sutures (ETHIBOND EXCEL polyester suture, 2-0, MH needle, X843H; Ethicon, Somerville, NJ, USA). All intraoperative cultures were negative, and the fragile tissue revealed an organizing hematoma lacking any myocardial tissue. She experienced prolonged respiratory failure, requiring tracheostomy and mechanical ventilation for 6 months, and was moved to the rehabilitation ward, but died 1 year after surgery due to pneumonia. Conclusions Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm formation is a notable late complication that should be carefully monitored during the postoperative follow-up after surgery for LVFWR. We encountered a case of a re-ruptured left ventricular pseudoaneurysm after a sutureless bovine pericardial patch repair. The possibility of re-rupture must be considered because the myocardial tissue beneath the pericardial patch might disappear and be replaced with an organizing hematoma.

title: Confluence Stones at the Junction of the Cystic Duct and an Aberrant Anterior Sectoral Bile Duct: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Confluence stones usually arise when gallstones impacted in the cystic duct migrate toward the biliary confluence. Surgical treatment can be technically demanding because of chronic inflammation and distorted anatomy. Confluence stones at the junction between the cystic duct and an aberrant bile duct are extremely rare. We report a successfully treated case of confluence stones arising at the junction of the cystic duct and an aberrant anterior sectoral bile duct with a communicating accessory bile duct. Case presentation A 38-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain, and biliary stones were detected. Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography demonstrated an aberrant anterior sectoral bile duct draining independently into the common bile duct. Biliary stones were identified both within this duct and at its junction with the cystic duct. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography confirmed the biliary anatomy and additionally revealed a communicating accessory bile duct between the anterior and posterior sectoral ducts. The stones within the distal portion of the aberrant duct were removed endoscopically, but the impacted confluence stones could not be extracted. Therefore, open surgery was performed. After exposure of the junction, the confluence stones were removed through a semicircumferential incision. Complete stone clearance was confirmed by intraoperative cholangioscopy and cholangiography. The patient was discharged on POD 11 with no bile leakage. At 14 months postoperatively, she remained asymptomatic and had experienced no episodes of cholangitis. Conclusions We report a rare case of confluence stones arising at the junction of the cystic duct and an aberrant anterior sectoral bile duct. Preoperative assessment of the drainage territory and intraoperative evaluation of the duct diameter, ischemia, and tissue fragility are essential for appropriate and safe repair of the bile duct defect. The repair strategy should not rely on presumed bypass flow through a communicating accessory bile duct because its functional capacity cannot be reliably predicted.

title: Pancreaticoduodenectomy after Laparoscopic Sleeve Gastrectomy with Preservation of Gastric Arterial Inflow: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Obesity is an established risk factor for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. As laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) has become increasingly prevalent, pancreatic surgeons may encounter malignancies in patients with a surgically altered gastric anatomy. Pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) after an LSG is rare and requires meticulous preoperative planning to prevent ischemic and anastomotic complications. Case presentation A 47-year-old man with morbid obesity (BMI 59.1 kg/m 2 ) underwent LSG. Twenty-three days later, obstructive jaundice led to the diagnosis of pancreatic head adenocarcinoma. After neoadjuvant chemotherapy and substantial weight reduction (BMI 34.9 kg/m 2 ), subtotal stomach-preserving pancreaticoduodenectomy with wedge resection of the superior mesenteric vein was performed. Preoperative CT confirmed the preservation and patency of both the left and right gastric arteries. The left gastric artery was preserved intraoperatively. Gastrojejunostomy was performed using a hand-sewn anastomosis between the greater curvature side of the sleeve stomach and the jejunum. The patient developed a grade B postoperative pancreatic fistula but was discharged with no ischemic complications. Conclusions PD after an LSG is feasible, but careful vascular assessment, a preplanned reconstruction strategy, consideration of the patient's metabolic and nutritional status, and careful intraoperative assessment of the remnant stomach may enhance surgical safety.

title: Resection of a Large Intra-Abdominal Desmoid Tumor with Preoperative Superior Mesenteric Artery Balloon Catheter Placement: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Large tumors occupying the abdominal cavity can hinder surgical exposure, particularly of the posterior aspect, increasing the risk of arterial bleeding. Because arterial hemostasis is difficult, hemodynamic instability may occur. This report describes the safe use of preoperative balloon catheter placement in the superior mesenteric artery (SMA), the tumor's primary feeding vessel, to control arterial bleeding through on-demand intraoperative occlusion. Case presentation A 40-year-old woman with a history of 2 cesarean sections presented with abdominal distension. An intra-abdominal mass was identified at another institution, and she was referred to our hospital. Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a large intra-abdominal mass supplied primarily by jejunal branches of the SMA. US-guided biopsy confirmed desmoid tumor. Chemotherapy was also considered; however, debulking surgery followed by chemotherapy was planned to relieve abdominal symptoms. Because the large tumor was expected to limit surgical exposure and increase the risk of intraoperative bleeding, an SMA balloon catheter was electively placed the day before surgery. During surgery, the balloon was inflated on demand by the anesthesiologist at the surgeon's direction before maneuvers carrying a risk of arterial bleeding. Tumor involvement of the small bowel mesentery, transverse mesocolon, small intestine, and duodenum required en bloc resection. As SMA involvement was confined to the segment distal to the ileocolic artery bifurcation, complete macroscopic resection was feasible while preserving approximately 200 cm of the small bowel. The resected specimen weighed 5660 g. Immunohistochemistry showed nuclear β-catenin positivity, confirming the diagnosis of desmoid tumor. Negative surgical margins achieved R0 resection. title: Long-Term Survival after Complete Resection of Local Duodenal Recurrence following Colon Cancer Surgery Using Laparoscopic and Endoscopic Cooperation: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperative surgery (LECS) enables accurate intraluminal localization and limited full-thickness resection while preserving gastrointestinal continuity. Although LECS has been used for selected primary duodenal tumors, its application to a postoperative duodenal recurrence of colorectal cancer has rarely been described. We report a case of localized duodenal recurrence after a right hemicolectomy that was completely resected using laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperation. Case presentation An 83-year-old man underwent a laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with a D3 lymph node dissection for advanced ascending colon cancer. Histopathological examination demonstrated a microscopically positive dissected margin on the duodenal side, indicating a microscopically positive margin (R1) resection. Nine months later, surveillance upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and contrast-enhanced CT revealed a solitary lesion in the second portion of the duodenum without distant metastasis or radiological pancreatic involvement. Endoscopic ultrasonography showed a lesion extending to the fourth layer. An upper gastrointestinal contrast study was not performed; instead, the location and local extent of the lesion were assessed by upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, endoscopic ultrasonography, and contrast-enhanced CT. Because the multimodal assessment indicated that complete local excision was technically achievable, LECS was performed. Intraoperative endoscopy delineated a wider intraluminal extent than was apparent from the serosal surface and guided an en bloc full-thickness resection. The defect was closed in the short-axis direction by a continuous full-thickness suturing. Intraoperative endoscopy confirmed the luminal patency and a negative leak test. Histopathological examination showed an adenocarcinoma involving the submucosa and muscularis propria without duodenal mucosal involvement. The adjacent muscularis propria was inverted toward the lumen, suggesting inward progression from the outer aspect of the duodenal wall. Together with the previous R1, these findings supported a localized recurrence from microscopic residual disease. The resection margins were negative, and the patient has remained disease-free for more than 5 years. Conclusions Laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperation enabled precise definition of the recurrent lesion, complete full-thickness local resection, and secure closure while preserving duodenal continuity. This approach may be useful for strictly localized duodenal recurrence when careful preoperative assessment indicates that complete local excision is achievable.

title: Gastric Glomus Tumor Mimicking a Neuroendocrine Tumor: A Case Report Highlighting Diagnostic Pitfalls.
abstract: Introduction Gastric glomus tumors (GGTs) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms arising from the modified smooth muscle cells of the glomus body. Their subepithelial location and pronounced hypervascularity overlap considerably with gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) on imaging and in small biopsy specimens, making an accurate preoperative diagnosis challenging; as a result, such lesions are frequently diagnosed after surgical resection. Case presentation A 38-year-old asymptomatic woman was found to have a 25-mm well-circumscribed, hypervascular submucosal lesion with a small central depression and minute ulceration in the upper gastric body during a routine health-screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD). Endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) demonstrated a heterogeneous hypoechoic mass arising from the third sonographic layer without evidence of muscularis propria invasion. Contrast-enhanced CT showed a hypervascular lesion with no regional lymphadenopathy or distant metastasis. Conventional forceps biopsies targeting the minute ulceration, evaluated with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining alone, were interpreted as consistent with a NET, leading to a provisional diagnosis of a type III gastric NET. Because of the diagnostic uncertainty surrounding the NET diagnosis, and because the EUS and CT showed no evidence of deep or nodal spread, the patient underwent laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperative surgery (LECS) with a local full-thickness gastric resection rather than upfront gastrectomy with lymphadenectomy, and the defect was repaired through a protective mini-laparotomy. Definitive histopathology demonstrated uniform round-to-spindle cells arranged in a perivascular sheet pattern within a myxoid stroma. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) showed focal positivity for α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) and negativity for KIT (CD117), CD34, chromogranin A, synaptophysin, desmin, and the S-100 protein, confirming a GGT. All surgical margins were negative, and no recurrence has been observed over 5 years of follow-up. Conclusions A GGT must be included in the differential diagnosis of hypervascular gastric subepithelial lesions (SELs), including those with a nested, NET-like architecture. H&E staining alone is insufficient for a definitive diagnosis; direct communication with the pathologist and comprehensive IHC profiling are indispensable. LECS is a favorable and effective organ-preserving strategy for localized gastric SELs when the diagnosis remains uncertain despite the preoperative evaluation.

title: Pancreatic Perivascular Epithelioid Cell Tumor: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Introduction Perivascular epithelioid cell tumors (PEComas) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms, and primary pancreatic PEComas are exceptionally uncommon. Owing to their rarity, the prognostic significance of their pathological features remains unclear. We report a resected case of pancreatic PEComa and review the literature to further characterize its clinicopathological features. Case presentation A 72-year-old woman presented with a gradually enlarging, 63-mm hypervascular tumor in the pancreatic body. Contrast-enhanced CT and MRI demonstrated a well-circumscribed hypervascular mass with central hypoenhancement, suggestive of coagulative necrosis. Endoscopic US-guided tissue acquisition suggested acinar cell carcinoma because of weak trypsin positivity, and distal pancreatectomy with regional lymph node dissection was performed. Histopathological examination of the resected specimen revealed epithelioid and spindle cells that were positive for HMB45 and Melan-A and weakly positive for α-smooth muscle actin, leading to a diagnosis of pancreatic PEComa. The patient remained disease-free at 18 months after surgery. We also reviewed 26 previously reported cases of pancreatic PEComa and re-evaluated those with sufficient pathological information according to the Folpe criteria. Metastasis developed in 1 tumor classified as malignant and 1 classified as having uncertain malignant potential. Coagulative necrosis and increased mitotic activity appeared to be more frequent in the 2 metastatic cases; however, the small number of events precluded conclusions regarding their prognostic significance or the predictive performance of the Folpe classification. Conclusions Pancreatic PEComa should be considered in the differential diagnosis of hypervascular pancreatic tumors with atypical immunophenotypic findings. Additional immunohistochemical staining for melanocytic markers may facilitate an accurate preoperative diagnosis. The prognostic significance of individual pathological features and the applicability of the Folpe classification to pancreatic PEComa remain uncertain and require evaluation in additional well-documented cases with long-term follow-up.

title: Surgical Resection of a Rapidly Enlarging Endotracheal Schwannoma under Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Support: A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction Primary tracheal schwannoma is an extremely rare benign tumor, and despite its typical slow growth, it can cause life-threatening airway obstruction as it enlarges. We report a case of an endotracheal schwannoma that exhibited rapid enlargement during the preoperative waiting period. The tumor was safely resected with veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (V-V ECMO) support because of the risk of complete airway obstruction. Case presentation A 73-year-old woman presented with hemoptysis. CT revealed a broad-based endotracheal tumor measuring 11 × 9 × 14 mm that was located 30 mm proximal to the carina. Bronchoscopic biopsy suggested benign schwannoma. The patient returned with worsening dyspnea and increased cough 2 weeks later. Follow-up CT showed rapid enlargement of the tumor to 17 × 12 × 21 mm, leaving a residual airway diameter of 4.2 mm. Given the risk of ventilation failure during the induction of general anesthesia, V-V ECMO was established while the patient was awake under local anesthesia. After adequate extracorporeal gas exchange was confirmed, general anesthesia was induced, followed by orotracheal intubation. Through a median sternotomy, the cervical and upper mediastinal trachea was exposed. The tumor-bearing tracheal segment was circumferentially resected, and primary end-to-end anastomosis was performed. The postoperative course was uncomplicated, and the patient remained recurrence-free at 12 months after surgery. Conclusions Although benign tracheal schwannomas are generally slow-growing, rapid enlargement can occur and potentially cause life-threatening airway obstruction. In patients with severe tracheal obstruction, planned establishment of V-V ECMO before induction of general anesthesia may provide an additional margin of safety during airway management and tracheal reconstruction.

title: Impact of FOSL1 polymorphisms and expression on disease progression in oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Oral tongue squamous cell carcinoma (OTSCC) is the most common subtype of oral cancer, with betel quid chewing, tobacco smoking, and alcohol consumption recognized as major risk factors. This study investigated the associations between FOSL1 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and disease susceptibility and clinicopathological characteristics in OTSCC patients. Three FOSL1 SNPs (rs637571, rs653914, and rs10896065) were genotyped in 377 male OTSCC patients and 1,194 controls using real-time polymerase chain reaction. The FOSL1 rs10896065 polymorphic T variant was significantly associated with advanced clinical stage (Stage III-IV; AOR = 1.663, 95% CI = 1.059-2.611, p = 0.027) and larger tumor size (AOR = 1.813, 95% CI = 1.162-2.831, p = 0.009). Among betel quid chewers, carriers of the CT+TT genotype showed significant associations with advanced clinical stage, larger tumor size, and moderate-to-poor tumor differentiation. Similar associations with advanced stage and greater tumor size were observed among smokers carrying the CT+TT genotype. Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas dataset further demonstrated that elevated FOSL1 mRNA expression was significantly associated with larger tumor size (T3-T4 vs. T1-T2, p = 0.0216). These findings suggest that the FOSL1 rs10896065 T allele is associated with advanced clinicopathological features in OTSCC patients, particularly among betel-quid chewers and smokers. FOSL1 polymorphisms may have potential as biomarkers associated with clinicopathological characteristics in OTSCC.

title: Overuse and False Restraint in Large Language Model Recommendations for Choosing Wisely Scenarios.
abstract: Background The Choosing Wisely initiative made recommendations where screening, testing, or treatment may be overused, with caveats around appropriate use. Clinicians are increasingly using large language models (LLMs). Objective To evaluate whether commercial LLMs appropriately call for restraint or action from scenarios based on Choosing Wisely recommendations. Design Benchmark evaluation. Fifteen Choosing Wisely recommendations were used to develop 225 scenarios (per recommendation, 10 in which restraint was appropriate and 5 in which action was appropriate). Six commercial LLMs (3 runs each) generated 4050 responses to the 225 scenarios, using a prompt from the clinician perspective. Setting Production application programming interfaces of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google from February to March 2026. Participants No human participants were involved. Measurements Co-primary outcomes were the overuse rate (endorsing action when restraint was appropriate) and the false restraint rate (withholding an appropriate action). Results The rate of LLM-recommended overuse was 5.4% (95% CI, 0.6% to 12.2%); LLMs did not recommend overuse in 8 of 15 recommendations. Two recommendations accounted for most LLM-recommended overuse: thyroid ultrasound for an incidental subcentimeter nodule (overuse recommended in 42.8% of LLM responses) and routine electrocardiography in low-risk adults (overuse recommended in 28.3% of LLM responses). The LLMs recommended overuse in 0.6% to 3.3% of responses for the remaining 5 recommendations. False restraint was rare (0.6% [CI, 0.1% to 1.2%]), was absent for 11 of 15 recommendations, and was highest for prostate-specific antigen screening (3.3%). Limitations Single prompts without follow-up; a benchmark rather than real-world use; responses classified by LLM judge with physician adjudication. Findings may not extend to consumer-facing use. Conclusion The LLMs rarely withheld recommendations for treatment when it was appropriate. Overuse was concentrated in 2 recommendations. Primary funding source None.

title: An Unusual Bilateral Presentation of Meigs' Syndrome in a Postmenopausal Woman: A Case Report.
abstract: Abstract Meigs' syndrome is a rare benign condition characterized by the triad of an ovarian tumor, ascites, and pleural effusion, often mimicking advanced ovarian malignancy. We report the case of a nulliparous woman in her late seventies who presented with a four-month history of progressive dyspnea, abdominal pain, and urinary frequency. Imaging revealed large bilateral solid adnexal masses measuring 17 cm and 15 cm, with no ascites detected initially. Tumor markers, including CA-125 (14 U/mL), were within normal limits. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated well-defined, non-enhancing solid masses without diffusion restriction, suggestive of benign ovarian stromal tumors. The Risk of Malignancy Index was 126, indicating low malignant potential. The patient underwent total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. Intraoperatively, two distinct ovarian tumors measuring approximately 8 cm each were identified, along with 300 mL of clear ascitic fluid, representing interval development not detected on prior imaging. Histopathological examination confirmed bilateral ovarian fibromas. Cytology of ascitic fluid was negative for malignancy. Postoperatively, ascites and pleural effusions resolved completely, confirming the diagnosis of bilateral Meigs' syndrome. At follow-up, the patient remained asymptomatic with no evidence of recurrence. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing Meigs' syndrome from ovarian malignancy, particularly in the presence of large bilateral masses. Integration of imaging characteristics, tumor markers, and risk stratification tools is essential to guide appropriate management and avoid unnecessary aggressive treatment.

title: Correlation of conventional histopathology and GeneXpert MTB/RIF in the diagnosis of spinal tuberculosis.
abstract: Introduction Spinal tuberculosis (STB) remains a significant health burden in tuberculosis-endemic regions, including India. Diagnosis is challenging because conventional microbiological methods, including acid-fast staining and mycobacterial culture, have limited sensitivity in paucibacillary disease. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of GeneXpert MTB/RIF in comparison with conventional histopathological examination (HPE) for the diagnosis of STB. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 64 patients with clinical and radiological suspicion of spinal tuberculosis who underwent transpedicular biopsy. Patients with definitive GeneXpert MTB/RIF and histopathological examination results were included. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 24.0 (IBM Corp., Armonk, NY, USA). Results Histopathology was positive in 46 (71.9%) patients, while GeneXpert MTB/RIF was positive in 63 (98.4%); both tests were positive in 45 (70.3%) cases. Compared with histopathology, GeneXpert demonstrated 97.83% sensitivity, 0% specificity, 71.43% positive predictive value, and 70.31% overall accuracy. The association between GeneXpert and HPE results was not statistically significant (χ² = 0.398, p = 0.528). Conclusion GeneXpert MTB/RIF is a rapid and sensitive adjunct to histopathology in the diagnosis of STB. However, the absence of specificity and the modest overall diagnostic accuracy observed in this study should warrant a cautious interpretation of this diagnostic tool.

title: Qualitative MRI Features for Differentiating GBM, Solitary Brain Metastasis, and Primary CNS Lymphoma: A Retrospective Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
abstract: Background Glioblastoma (GBM), solitary brain metastasis (SM), and primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) are important malignant brain tumors that may exhibit overlapping imaging features, making preoperative differentiation challenging. Although conventional MRI (cMRI) is widely available and routinely used in clinical practice, comprehensive comparative evaluation of cMRI features for differentiating these three entities remains limited. Purpose This study aimed to identify conventional MRI features distinguishing GBM, SM, and PCNSL, and to develop a diagnostic algorithm for initial evaluation. Material and methods This retrospective study included 108 patients (59 GBM, 24 SM, 25 PCNSL) who underwent pre-operative 3T brain MRI between May 2021 and May 2025, with histopathologic confirmation. The imaging features were compared using appropriate statistical tests. Statistically significant qualitative variables were then entered into a classification model built with the CHAID (Chi-square Automatic Interaction Detection) growing method. Results Significant differences were observed across tumor types in lesion location, border characteristics, enhancement patterns, and specific signs such as the notch sign, worm-like sign, and intra-tumoral vascular enhancement (all p < 0.05). PCNSLs commonly showed homogeneous enhancement and regular margins, while GBM and SM demonstrated heterogeneous ring enhancement, necrosis, and hemorrhage. The CHAID decision tree achieved an overall accuracy of 80.6%, with class-specific accuracies of 83.3% for GBM, 86.1% for SM, and 91.7% for PCNSL. Conclusions The proposed decision tree offers a practical tool for diagnostic orientation and treatment planning, particularly in settings without access to advanced imaging techniques.

title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease phenotypes and 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: Background The prognostic significance of lean metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) in patients with obstructive coronary artery disease remains uncertain. We evaluated 1-year cardiovascular outcomes in lean versus non-lean MAFLD. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 193 adults with MAFLD and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-defined obstructive coronary artery disease at Thong Nhat Hospital, Vietnam. Lean MAFLD was defined as a body mass index <23 kg/m² and non-lean MAFLD as a body mass index ≥23 kg/m². The primary outcome was the first expanded major adverse cardiovascular event (eMACE) within 365 days, including ischemia-driven coronary revascularization. Planned first percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) after baseline CCTA was included. Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Results During follow-up, 115 patients (59.6%) experienced eMACE. The eMACE rate was higher in lean than in non-lean MAFLD (86.2% vs 54.9%, P=0.002). Among these cases, recorded components were revascularization (108), myocardial infarction (13), unstable angina (26), acute heart failure (1), stroke (0), and cardiovascular death (0); components overlapped. These counts do not establish first-event attribution. Lean MAFLD remained associated with eMACE after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary artery disease (adjusted HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.32-3.26, P=0.002). Conclusions Among patients with MAFLD and obstructive coronary artery disease, lean MAFLD was associated with a higher 1-year hazard of eMACE than non-lean MAFLD, after adjustment for age, sex, and multivessel coronary disease. The small lean group and inclusion of planned revascularization limit extrapolation to non-revascularization events, confirmation in larger cohorts is needed.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously. Objectives To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer. Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry. Conclusions Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

title: [X-ray-guided lung puncture navigation integrating direct linear transformation-Gauss-Newton method and marker-free registration].
abstract: Percutaneous transthoracic needle biopsy (PTNB) is an important modality for the qualitative diagnosis of lung cancer, which relies on medical-image guidance. X-ray equipment features wide availability and low radiation dose; nevertheless, X-ray-guided PTNB requires repeated calibration using physical calibrators. Accordingly, this paper proposes an X-ray-guided lung puncture navigation method integrating the direct linear transformation-Gauss-Newton method (DLT-GNM) and marker-free registration. Preoperatively, initial imaging parameters are acquired via fluoroscopic calibration. Intraoperatively, a binocular camera tracks the spatial pose of the C-arm in real time to virtually reconstruct calibration points. DLT-GNM is employed to solve the projection model and realize marker-free real-time navigation. Respiratory phantom experiments show that the overall localization error is (0.38 ± 0.25) mm under matched respiratory phases. It is verified that this method delivers high accuracy and simple operation, and possesses favorable clinical application potential for cases with large lesions or identifiable targets clearly visualized under X-ray fluoroscopy.

title: [Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with double-bundle artificial ligament based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism: a comparative study with single-bundle reconstruction].
abstract: Objective To investigate the surgical method of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction with double-bundle artificial ligaments based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism, and to compare its short-term effectiveness with traditional single-bundle reconstruction. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 45 patients with complete ACL rupture who met the selection criteria and were treated between October 2022 and October 2025. Based on anatomical measurement results and surgical technique selection, patients were divided into a single-bundle reconstruction group (29 cases, receiving traditional over-the-top isometric single-bundle reconstruction) and a double-bundle reconstruction group [16 cases, receiving four-dimensional impingement free ACL double-bundle reconstruction (over-the-top anteromedial bundle+low posterolateral bundle)]. Baseline data-including age, injured side, cause of injury, concomitant meniscus injury, and preoperative Lysholm score, International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) score, and Tegner score-showed no significant difference between the two groups ( P >0.05); however, the difference in gender distribution between the two groups was significant ( P <0.05). Operation time, complications, knee range of motion, and the results of the Lachman test, anterior drawer test, and pivot-shift test were recorded. Knee function was evaluated using the Lysholm, IKDC, and Tegner scores preoperatively and at last follow-up, and the proportion of patients returning to pre-injury sports activity levels was calculated. Postoperative three-dimensional CT was performed to evaluate bone tunnel placement and graft-to-tunnel congruence. Results Operations were successfully completed in both groups, with the operation time in the double-bundle reconstruction group being significantly longer than that in the single-bundle reconstruction group ( P <0.05). All patients were followed up 6-13 months, with an average of 8.5 months. Patients in both groups resumed immediate postoperative knee range of motion reached 0°-135°, and normal independent walking at 2 weeks postoperatively. At last follow-up, the Lachman test and anterior drawer test were negative in all patients; the pivot-shift test was negative in all cases in the double-bundle reconstruction group, whereas 3 cases (all grade Ⅰ) were positive in the single-bundle reconstruction group, with no significant difference in the positive rate of the pivot-shift test between the two groups ( P >0.05). At last follow-up, the proportion of patients returning to pre-injury sports activity levels was significantly higher in the double-bundle reconstruction group than in the single-bundle reconstruction group ( P <0.05). Both the IKDC and Tegner scores showed significant improvement compared with preoperative values in the two groups ( P <0.05), while the Lysholm scores showed no significant difference when compared with preoperative values ( P >0.05). There was no significant difference in the pre- to post-operative change values of each score between the two groups ( P >0.05). Postoperative three-dimensional CT demonstrated that the distance between the margins of the anterior and posterior bone tunnels in the double-bundle reconstruction group was more than 5 mm, with no evidence of tunnel fracture or posterior cruciate ligament impingement; MRI showed favorable graft morphology without signs of impingement. During the follow-up, no severe complications such as graft laxity, rupture, or synovitis occurred in either group. Conclusion Under the guarantee of strict anatomical screening, artificial ligament double-bundle reconstruction based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism shows a favorable clinical trend in restoring rotational stability, with pivot-shift control superior to that of single-bundle reconstruction. Combined with a higher rate of return to sports, it holds significant clinical value for athletic populations seeking early, high-quality rehabilitation. However, strict indication screening based on individualized anatomical conditions is essential for this surgical procedure.
originalAbstract:
Objective

To investigate the surgical method of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction with double-bundle artificial ligaments based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism, and to compare its short-term effectiveness with traditional single-bundle reconstruction.

Methods

A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 45 patients with complete ACL rupture who met the selection criteria and were treated between October 2022 and October 2025. Based on anatomical measurement results and surgical technique selection, patients were divided into a single-bundle reconstruction group (29 cases, receiving traditional over-the-top isometric single-bundle reconstruction) and a double-bundle reconstruction group [16 cases, receiving four-dimensional impingement free ACL double-bundle reconstruction (over-the-top anteromedial bundle+low posterolateral bundle)]. Baseline data-including age, injured side, cause of injury, concomitant meniscus injury, and preoperative Lysholm score, International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) score, and Tegner score-showed no significant difference between the two groups ( P>0.05); however, the difference in gender distribution between the two groups was significant ( P<0.05). Operation time, complications, knee range of motion, and the results of the Lachman test, anterior drawer test, and pivot-shift test were recorded. Knee function was evaluated using the Lysholm, IKDC, and Tegner scores preoperatively and at last follow-up, and the proportion of patients returning to pre-injury sports activity levels was calculated. Postoperative three-dimensional CT was performed to evaluate bone tunnel placement and graft-to-tunnel congruence.

Results

Operations were successfully completed in both groups, with the operation time in the double-bundle reconstruction group being significantly longer than that in the single-bundle reconstruction group ( P<0.05). All patients were followed up 6-13 months, with an average of 8.5 months. Patients in both groups resumed immediate postoperative knee range of motion reached 0°-135°, and normal independent walking at 2 weeks postoperatively. At last follow-up, the Lachman test and anterior drawer test were negative in all patients; the pivot-shift test was negative in all cases in the double-bundle reconstruction group, whereas 3 cases (all grade Ⅰ) were positive in the single-bundle reconstruction group, with no significant difference in the positive rate of the pivot-shift test between the two groups ( P>0.05). At last follow-up, the proportion of patients returning to pre-injury sports activity levels was significantly higher in the double-bundle reconstruction group than in the single-bundle reconstruction group ( P<0.05). Both the IKDC and Tegner scores showed significant improvement compared with preoperative values in the two groups ( P<0.05), while the Lysholm scores showed no significant difference when compared with preoperative values ( P>0.05). There was no significant difference in the pre- to post-operative change values of each score between the two groups ( P>0.05). Postoperative three-dimensional CT demonstrated that the distance between the margins of the anterior and posterior bone tunnels in the double-bundle reconstruction group was more than 5 mm, with no evidence of tunnel fracture or posterior cruciate ligament impingement; MRI showed favorable graft morphology without signs of impingement. During the follow-up, no severe complications such as graft laxity, rupture, or synovitis occurred in either group.

Conclusion

Under the guarantee of strict anatomical screening, artificial ligament double-bundle reconstruction based on four-dimensional impingement free mechanism shows a favorable clinical trend in restoring rotational stability, with pivot-shift control superior to that of single-bundle reconstruction. Combined with a higher rate of return to sports, it holds significant clinical value for athletic populations seeking early, high-quality rehabilitation. However, strict indication screening based on individualized anatomical conditions is essential for this surgical procedure.

title: [Effectiveness comparison of one-hole split endoscopy and unilateral biportal endoscopy discectomy via the superior articular process approach for L 5 , S 1 far lateral lumbar disc herniation].
abstract: Objective To compare the effectiveness between one-hole split endoscopy(OSE) and unilateral biportal endoscopy (UBE) discectomy via the superior articular process approach for L 5 , S 1 far lateral lumbar disc herniation (FLLDH). Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on the clinical data of 98 patients with L 5 , S 1 FLLDH who met the selection criteria and were admitted between January 2021 and December 2024. The patients were divided into an OSE group (52 cases) and a UBE group (46 cases) according to the surgical procedure. There was no significant difference in baseline data between the two groups ( P >0.05), such as age, gender, side, body mass index, preoperative anterior-posterior translation distance (ATD), disc height (DH), lumbar lordosis angle (LLA), visual analogue scale (VAS) scores for low back pain and leg pain, and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Operation time, intraoperative blood loss, intraoperative fluoroscopy frequency, incision length, and postoperative hospital stay were recorded. Three-dimensional lumbar models were reconstructed, and the proportion of resected superior articular process bone volume of S 1 was calculated by measuring the bone volume of the S 1 superior articular process before and after surgery. Clinical outcomes were evaluated using VAS scores, ODI, while lumbar stability was assessed by ATD, DH, and LLA measurements. Results All patients successfully underwent operation. The OSE group had significantly shorter operation time, less intraoperative blood loss, and smaller incision length than the UBE group ( P <0.05); no significant difference was found in intraoperative fluoroscopy frequency or postoperative hospital stay between the two groups ( P >0.05). No severe neurological or vascular injuries occurred intraoperatively in either group, mild dural tears were observed in 2 patients in the UBE group. All patients were followed up 12-18 months, with an average of 14.7 months. In both groups, VAS scores and ODI at each postoperative time point decreased significantly when compared with preoperative values, with further improvement over time, and the differences among time points were significant ( P <0.05). Intergroup comparisons showed that, except for a higher low back pain VAS score in the UBE group at postoperative 3 days ( P <0.05), there was no significant difference in VAS scores or ODI between the two groups at the other time points ( P >0.05). At last follow-up, there was no significant difference in ATD, DH, and LLA within each group when compared with preoperative values ( P >0.05). No significant intergroup difference was observed in the changes of ATD, DH, and LLA from preoperation to postoperation between the two groups ( P >0.05). There was a significant difference in the proportion of resected superior articular processbone volume of S 1 between the two groups ( P <0.05), but the proportion in both groups were less than 35%. There was no recurrence during the follow-up. Conclusion Both OSE and UBE approaches for lumbar discectomy via the superior articular process can achieve satisfactory effectiveness for treating L 5 , S 1 FLLDH, preserve more important bone of the S 1 superior articular process, which is conducive to maintaining lumbar stability. Compared with UBE, the OSE technique offers advantages of shorter operation time, less trauma, and reduced blood loss.

title: [Comparative study on effectiveness of two fixation methods in treatment of mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries].
abstract: Objective To compare the effectiveness of open reduction with screw internal fixation versus primary arthrodesis for mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 45 patients (45 feet) with mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries, who met the selective criteria between June 2019 and June 2022. Among them, 23 patients were treated with primary tarsometatarsal arthrodesis (arthrodesis group), and 22 patients received open reduction with screw internal fixation (screw group). There was no significant difference between groups ( P >0.05) in age, gender, body mass index, injured side, interval from injury to operation, Myerson classification, and preoperative visual analogue scale (VAS) score, American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, 36-Item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36) score, the distance between the medial cuneiform and the second metatarsal (C1-M2), the distance between first and second metatarsal (M1-M2), step-off sign (SOS) displacement, and talus-first metatarsal angle (Meary angle). Operation time, incision length, intraoperative fluoroscopy frequency, intraoperative blood loss, time to initial weight-bearing, time to full weight-bearing, and postoperative complications during follow-up were recorded and compared. Pain and functional recovery were evaluated using VAS, AOFAS, and SF-36 scores. Radiographic parameters including C1-M2, M1-M2, SOS displacement, and Meary angle were measured during follow-up. Intergroup differences in the changes of the all outcome indicators from preoperative to last follow-up were also compared. Results All patients underwent successful operation. The arthrodesis group had significantly longer operation time, longer incision length, more intraoperative fluoroscopy exposures, and greater intraoperative blood loss compared with the screw group ( P <0.05). All patients were followed up 24-36 months (mean, 27.6 months). No significant intergroup difference was found in time to initial weight-bearing or time to full weight-bearing ( P >0.05). At last follow-up, the indicators for function, pain, and imaging in both groups significantly improved compared with those before operation ( P <0.05). The arthrodesis group achieved significantly greater changes of AOFAS score, VAS score, SF-36 score, and Meary angle than the screw group ( P <0.05). No significant intergroup difference was found in the changes of C1-M2, M1-M2, and SOS ( P >0.05). The incidence of complication was significantly lower in arthrodesis group (8.6%, 2/23) than in screw group (36.3%, 8/22) ( P <0.05). Conclusion For mid-column plantar-flexion Lisfranc injuries, primary tarsometatarsal arthrodesis yields better functional recovery and pain relief compared with open reduction and screw internal fixation.

title: [Effectiveness of arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous tendon graft for irreparable massive rotator cuff tears].
abstract: Objective To evaluate effectiveness of arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous tendon graft in treatment of irreparable massive rotator cuff tears (IMRCT). Methods A retrospective case series study was conducted on 32 patients with IMRCT treated between July 2022 and December 2023. All patients underwent arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous peroneus longus tendon graft. There were 11 males and 21 females, aged 49-76 years (mean, 65 years). The clinical symptoms were joint pain accompanied by limited mobility and abduction weakness. The duration of preoperative symptoms ranged from 3 to 24 months (mean, 9 months). Pain was assessed using the visual analogue scale (VAS) score, and shoulder function was evaluated using the modified University of California at Los Angeles (UCLA) score and the Constant-Murley score before operation and at 3, 6, 12 months after operation. MRI was performed during follow-up to assess graft integrity. Complications were recorded. Results The operation time ranged from 75 to 130 minutes, with a mean of 90 minutes. All incisions healed by first intention, and no significant complication or adverse reaction was observed. All patients were followed up 12-24 months (mean, 16.5 months). All postoperative scores improved significantly when compared with preoperative values ( P <0.05). Pain and function continued to improve over time; no significant difference was observed in the modified UCLA scores among 6 months, 12 months, and last follow-up, nor in any scores between 12 months and last follow-up ( P >0.05); all other pairwise comparisons showed significant differences ( P <0.05). At last follow-up, shoulder function was rated as excellent in 12 cases, good in 18 cases, and poor in 2 cases according to the modified UCLA scoring system, yielding an excellent-to-good rate of 93.8%. MRI follow-up demonstrated intact reconstructed rotator cuff structures in 29 patients, with a healing rate of 90.6% (29/32). Conclusion Arthroscopic grid-pattern dynamic rotator cuff reconstruction using autologous tendon graft is effective for IMRCT, significantly alleviating pain, improving shoulder range of motion, and restoring both functional and structural integrity, without major complication or adverse reaction.

title: Comparison of Data-Driven Phenotyping Systems for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Implications for Treatment Response.
abstract: Background Although emerging classification systems address the pathophysiological heterogeneity of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), the implications of these subtypes for treatment responses remain unclear. We systematically evaluated three phenotyping frameworks for stratifying responses to lifestyle management. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 618 patients with MASLD who received 48 weeks of guideline-based lifestyle management. The classification systems assessed were metabolic clusters-mild obesity/dyslipidemia-associated MASLD (MODM), age-related MASLD (AM), severe insulin resistance-associated MASLD, high lipoprotein(a)-associated MASLD (HLPAM), and severe mixed hyperlipidemia-associated MASLD (SMHLM); hepatic and cardiometabolic traits (control, liver-specific, and cardiometabolic); and biochemical patterns (hepatocellular, mixed, and cholestatic). The primary endpoints were responses in magnetic resonance imaging-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) (≥30% relative liver fat reduction), alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (≥17 IU/L decrease), and liver stiffness measurements (LSM) (≥1-stage improvement in the LSM-defined fibrosis stage). Results Metabolic clusters demonstrated significantly greater temporal stability than the hepatic and cardiometabolic trait and biochemical pattern systems (62.8% vs. 56.6% vs. 53.4%, P =0.003). The HLPAM cluster demonstrated an attenuated MRI-PDFF response (odds ratio [OR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.15 to 0.79), while the AM cluster showed a lower ALT response (OR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.18 to 0.62), and the MODM cluster displayed a superior LSM response compared to the others (all P <0.05). Moreover, the liver-specific cluster showed better MRI-PDFF, ALT, and LSM responses than the control cluster. However, biochemical patterns selectively stratified ALT responses, with the hepatocellular pattern demonstrating a greater response than the mixed and cholestatic patterns. Conclusion Metabolic cluster-based MASLD subtypes exhibited differential responses to lifestyle management, supporting the integration of metabolic subtyping into clinical algorithms to optimize management.

title: Three-dimensional coded aperture imaging system proposed for early breast cancer detection using low tumor-to-background ratio.
abstract: Coded aperture (CA) based image formation methods have been used in medical imaging for the past two decades. However, no commercially available Single Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT) CA camera technology has been developed yet. This study investigated the lower tumor-to-background ratio (TBR) in 3D breast reconstruction with tumors. TBR is a potential factor for evaluating the malignancy of breast cancer because of its correlation with lesion size. The CA-based SPECT camera uses an iterative reconstruction algorithm called Maximum Likelihood Expectation Maximization (MLEM) with a mosaic Modified Uniformly Redundant Array (MURA) mask and anti-mask dual reconstruction. The background noise and intrinsic artifacts are suppressed by subtracting mask reconstructed images from the anti-mask images, thereby reducing the non-uniformity in the background. The reconstructed slices are then stacked to create a three-dimensional representation of the breast phantom. By employing a TBR of 5:1, mosaic MURA mask anti-mask subtraction has enhanced the quality of the reconstructed images and made it possible to detect breast lesions with a diameter of 4 mm. Furthermore, rather than using a sinogram, the proposed method can create a 3D breast phantom from a single projection. Simulation results suggest the feasibility of detecting 4 mm lesions at TBR = 5:1 using a single-projection mosaic MURA coded aperture system. Clinical validation is required to confirm translation to patient imaging.

title: Improving Radiological Quality of Proximal Femoral Nail Antirotation Fixation for Intertrochanteric Femoral Fractures: A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit of Reduction Quality, Tip-Apex Distance, and Helical Blade Position.
abstract: Background The technical quality of proximal femoral nail antirotation (PFNA) fixation for intertrochanteric femoral fractures is influenced by fracture reduction and implant positioning. Reduction quality, tip-apex distance (TAD), and helical blade position are important immediate postoperative radiological indicators of fixation quality. This closed-loop clinical audit evaluated these parameters and assessed changes following targeted quality-improvement interventions. Aim To evaluate and improve the immediate postoperative radiological quality of PFNA fixation for intertrochanteric femoral fractures by comparing reduction quality, TAD, and helical blade position between baseline and re-audit cycles. Methods A retrospective baseline audit included 21 consecutive patients with intertrochanteric femoral fractures treated with PFNA between February 4, 2025, and February 3, 2026. Immediate postoperative anteroposterior (AP) and lateral radiographs were assessed for fracture reduction using predefined radiological criteria, TAD with correction for radiographic magnification, and helical blade position using the Cleveland index. Following review of the baseline findings, targeted quality-improvement interventions were implemented between April and May 2026. These included case-based discussion of reduction techniques, reinforcement of intraoperative TAD assessment, teaching on optimal blade positioning using the Cleveland index, and reinforcement of key PFNA technical principles. Following a post-intervention implementation period, 18 additional PFNA cases were assessed from June 2026 using the same eligibility criteria, radiological definitions, and outcome indicators. Between-cycle comparisons were performed using appropriate exact statistical tests for categorical variables and Welch's independent-samples t-test for mean TAD. Results At baseline, good reduction was achieved in 10/21 (47.6%) cases, TAD <25 mm in 14/21 (66.7%), and ideal blade positioning in 14/21 (66.7%), while poor reduction occurred in 4/21 (19.0%). At re-audit, good reduction increased to 12/18 (66.7%), representing an absolute increase of 19.0 percentage points, while ideal blade positioning increased to 14/18 (77.8%), an increase of 11.1 percentage points. Poor reduction decreased to 0/18 (0%). Achievement of TAD <25 mm increased modestly to 13/18 (72.2%), while mean TAD decreased from 23.6 ± 4.3 mm to 21.7 ± 3.2 mm. None of the principal between-cycle differences reached statistical significance. Conclusion Following targeted quality-improvement interventions, favorable changes were observed in fracture reduction and helical blade positioning, including elimination of poor reductions, while achievement of TAD <25 mm remained approximately 72%. Although the between-cycle differences were not statistically significant, the findings indicate encouraging quality-improvement trends and identify TAD optimization as an important target for subsequent audit cycles. Continued radiographic review, intraoperative attention to reduction and implant positioning, and periodic re-audit are recommended.

Between-cycle comparisons were performed using appropriate exact statistical tests for categorical variables and Welch's independent-samples t-test for mean TAD. Results At baseline, good reduction was achieved in 10/21 (47.6%) cases, TAD <25 mm in 14/21 (66.7%), and ideal blade positioning in 14/21 (66.7%), while poor reduction occurred in 4/21 (19.0%). At re-audit, good reduction increased to 12/18 (66.7%), representing an absolute increase of 19.0 percentage points, while ideal blade positioning increased to 14/18 (77.8%), an increase of 11.1 percentage points. Poor reduction decreased to 0/18 (0%). Achievement of TAD <25 mm increased modestly to 13/18 (72.2%), while mean TAD decreased from 23.6 ± 4.3 mm to 21.7 ± 3.2 mm. None of the principal between-cycle differences reached statistical significance. Conclusion Following targeted quality-improvement interventions, favorable changes were observed in fracture reduction and helical blade positioning, including elimination of poor reductions, while achievement of TAD <25 mm remained approximately 72%. Although the between-cycle differences were not statistically significant, the findings indicate encouraging quality-improvement trends and identify TAD optimization as an important target for subsequent audit cycles. Continued radiographic review, intraoperative attention to reduction and implant positioning, and periodic re-audit are recommended.

title: Reconciling Extent of Resection and Residual Tumor Volume in Glioblastoma: Sources of Discordance and a Proposed Reporting Framework.
abstract: Extent of resection (EOR) and residual tumor volume (RV) are among the few modifiable prognostic factors in glioblastoma (GBM), yet their interpretation remains complicated by substantial methodological heterogeneity. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary literature on EOR and RV as prognostic metrics in adult IDH-wild-type GBM, drawing on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science (January 2000-March 2026), and proposes a standardized reporting framework to improve cross-study comparability. Although both metrics are consistently associated with survival, apparent disagreement between EOR- and RV-based studies largely reflects methodological rather than genuine biological discordance. Key sources of heterogeneity include inconsistent terminology (18 distinct terms identified across six decades of literature, only about half with explicit thresholds), variable postoperative MRI timing, differing segmentation methods, inconsistent definitions of contrast-enhancing versus non-enhancing tumor compartments, evolving WHO molecular classification, and inadequate adjustment for confounding by indication, tumor location, and treatment factors. The Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO)-resect classification represents an important advance toward standardization and has undergone independent revalidation, but definitional inconsistency persists more broadly. Building on these findings, this review proposes an author-derived, ten-domain reporting framework spanning study population, patient and tumor characteristics, surgical approach, imaging acquisition, segmentation methodology, EOR/RV calculation, molecular classification, confounder adjustment, statistical methods, and outcome reporting, intended to complement rather than replace existing standards such as Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) and Transparent Reporting of a Multivariable Prediction Model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis (TRIPOD). This framework has not undergone formal Delphi consensus or prospective validation and should be regarded as a preliminary proposal. Standardized, transparent reporting, potentially supported by emerging AI-based segmentation and reporting tools, may help reconcile apparently conflicting findings and strengthen future evidence synthesis regarding surgical cytoreduction in GBM.

title: When Irrigation Flows the Wrong Way: Intraoperative Regurgitation Through an Enterovesical Fistula.
abstract: Enterovesical fistulas complicate inflammatory bowel disease, particularly after restorative proctocolectomy with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis, creating pathways that may complicate endoscopic urological procedures performed under continuous irrigation. A 33-year-old man (61 kg; body mass index 18.8 kg/m²) with unclassified pancolitis (no histological features of Crohn disease in the colectomy specimen) had undergone restorative proctocolectomy with an ileal J-pouch, defunctioning loop ileostomy and ileal pouch-anal anastomosis, with repeated failed interventions for a chronic enterovesical fistula. He underwent elective laser cystolithotripsy and suprapubic catheter exchange. After induction with fentanyl, lidocaine, propofol and rocuronium, the airway was managed with a size 4 i-gel (Intersurgical Ltd, Wokingham, UK), without an orogastric tube in its gastric channel, in the lithotomy position, with gravity-fed 0.9% saline irrigation. One hour and 23 minutes after the start of surgery, clear fluid appeared at the oropharynx. The oropharynx was suctioned, the trachea was intubated, and a nasogastric tube was placed; a second episode followed two minutes later. Irrigation was stopped. The ileostomy appliance, empty at induction, was completely distended with clear fluid, and irrigation return through the cystostomy was markedly reduced. Core temperature on admission to the intermediate care unit was 33.0 °C. Ventilatory parameters, auscultation, arterial blood gas analysis, and chest radiography showed no evidence of aspiration. He was discharged on postoperative day 7. We propose that the regurgitated fluid was predominantly irrigation fluid that had migrated retrogradely through the fistula into the ileal pouch and small bowel. To our knowledge, this mechanism has not been described previously. Fistulous urinary-gastrointestinal anatomy warrants treatment as an aspiration risk factor in its own right, with gastric-channel drainage whenever a supraglottic device is used, and deliberate monitoring of irrigation input, drainage return, stomal output, and core temperature.

title: Colonic Angiosarcoma 16 Years After Pelvic Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: A Case Report.
abstract: Angiosarcomas are rare and aggressive malignant neoplasms of vascular or lymphatic endothelial origin, accounting for approximately 2% of soft-tissue sarcomas. They occur predominantly in the skin and superficial soft tissues, particularly in the head and neck region and the breast, whereas gastrointestinal involvement is exceptionally rare. Previous radiotherapy is a well-established risk factor for secondary angiosarcoma. However, radiation-associated gastrointestinal angiosarcomas are extremely uncommon and have been reported predominantly in the small bowel. We report the case of a 55-year-old woman who presented with abdominal pain, hemorrhagic ascites, intermittent rectal bleeding, severe anemia, anorexia, and weight loss 16 years after pelvic radiotherapy and cisplatin-based chemotherapy for cervical squamous cell carcinoma. Computed tomography revealed circumferential thickening of the cecum and right colon with abundant hyperdense ascites. Colonoscopy showed an obstructing, ulcerated, and contact-bleeding mass involving the cecum and right colon. Histopathological examination of endoscopic biopsies revealed a poorly differentiated malignant vascular neoplasm. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for cluster of differentiation (CD)31 and CD34 and negative for cytokeratin, CD3, CD20, and Human Herpesvirus (HHV)8, with a Ki-67 proliferation index of 40%, supporting the diagnosis of colonic angiosarcoma. Surgical resection was considered; however, the patient developed a massive bilateral pulmonary embolism and died seven days after admission. Given the prolonged latency and the histological distinction from the primary cervical carcinoma, a possible radiation-associated etiology was considered. Nevertheless, the original radiotherapy plan was unavailable, preventing definitive confirmation that the tumor arose within the irradiated field. This case highlights the diagnostic difficulty, aggressive clinical course, and poor prognosis of colonic angiosarcoma following pelvic radiotherapy.

title: Solid Pseudopapillary Neoplasm of the Pancreatic Tail With Splenic Hilar Involvement: A Case Report.
abstract: Solid pseudopapillary epithelial neoplasm (SPEN) is a rare pancreatic epithelial tumour that predominantly affects young women and is characterised by low malignant potential and favourable prognosis following complete surgical resection. A 28-year-old woman presented with intermittent left upper abdominal pain and loss of appetite for one month. Physical examination and laboratory investigations, including tumour markers, were unremarkable. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 7.4 × 7.0 × 6.4 cm well-defined cystic lesion with solid components arising from the pancreatic tail, suggestive of SPEN. The patient underwent distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy due to splenic hilar involvement. Histopathological examination and immunohistochemistry confirmed SPEN, demonstrating β-catenin and progesterone receptor positivity with a Ki-67 index <1%. SPEN is an uncommon pancreatic tumour that typically presents with non-specific symptoms, often leading to delayed diagnosis. Characteristic imaging findings combined with histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation are essential for accurate diagnosis. Complete surgical resection remains the treatment of choice and is associated with favourable outcomes. SPEN should be considered in young women presenting with pancreatic cystic lesions and vague abdominal symptoms. Complete surgical excision by distal pancreatectomy with splenectomy can achieve excellent oncological outcomes, even in cases with splenic hilar involvement.
